articles.title: OCBC: Markets can absorb a 25-bps Fed rate hike - IDNFinancials
articles.summary: OCBC: Markets can absorb a 25-bps Fed rate hike  IDNFinancials
articles.full_text:
JAKARTA - PT Bank OCBC NISP Tbk (NISP) has urged investors to monitor developments in US inflation, as these could influence the Federal Reserve's (The Fed) interest rate policy, capital flows and exchange rates in emerging markets, including the rupiah.
OCBC Group Chief Economist and Head of Research Selena Ling said US inflation was one of the key indicators investors should watch amid global economic uncertainty.
"Inflation will determine how long interest rates remain elevated. This, in turn, will affect capital flows, exchange rates, including the rupiah, as well as financing costs for businesses and households," Selena said at an OCBC media briefing in Jakarta on Tuesday (3 November).
According to her, markets expect the Fed could still raise interest rates by 25 basis points at its December 2026 meeting. However, the direction of monetary policy beyond that decision will depend on inflation developments.
Selena believes markets could still adjust if the Fed raises rates by just 25 basis points in December and subsequently keeps them unchanged for an extended period.
Conversely, more aggressive rate increases extending into 2027 could place greater pressure on global financial markets, particularly emerging economies.
Beyond US inflation, investors should also monitor geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and Ukraine. Prolonged conflicts could keep energy prices elevated and increase uncertainty across global supply chains.
Selena said these uncertainties meant investors needed to prepare strategies to manage various risks that could occur simultaneously, a phenomenon known as a polycrisis.
In such conditions, investors are advised to maintain liquidity and diversify their portfolios to reduce asset concentration risks.
"Investors need to remain flexible, maintain sufficient liquidity for future needs, while continuing to invest and seek opportunities," she said.
Diversification can be achieved across different asset classes, industry sectors, markets and currencies. This strategy is considered helpful in managing risks while maintaining flexibility as market conditions change.
Selena also cautioned investors against making decisions based on short-term market volatility. Asset allocation should be aligned with each investor's financial objectives, risk profile and investment horizon.
These global risks are also a concern for businesses. Selena believes companies need to strengthen supply chain resilience by reassessing their suppliers, target markets and business partners.
According to her, companies can no longer rely solely on just-in-time strategies, which focus on timely deliveries. They also need to establish alternative supply arrangements through a just-in-case approach to anticipate potential disruptions.
Meanwhile, Selena highlighted the sustainability of the artificial intelligence (AI) investment cycle. Several Asian countries are integrated into the semiconductor, data centre and cloud computing supply chains that support the global AI industry.
However, an investment slowdown in these sectors could affect economic growth, revenues and job creation in countries dependent on AI supply chains.
For Indonesia, Selena said economic resilience was also supported by adequate foreign exchange reserves. The country's reserves stood at US$146.3 billion at the end of September 2026, equivalent to 5.3 months of imports.
She added that fiscal discipline and the government's ability to maintain macroeconomic stability were crucial to sustaining investor confidence amid global volatility.
Selena stressed that investors should maintain a long-term strategy while ensuring adequate liquidity and adjusting their portfolios to match their individual risk tolerance. (DH/LM)

articles.title: Kazimir Warns of Further ECB Rate Hikes as Digital Euro Plans Advance - Coin Edition
articles.summary: Kazimir Warns of Further ECB Rate Hikes as Digital Euro Plans Advance  Coin Edition
articles.full_text:
- Kazimir warns that persistent inflation could require further ECB interest rate hikes.
- Rising energy and food prices, alongside a weaker euro, could increase inflationary pressure.
- The ECB plans to launch a 12-month digital euro pilot in the second half of 2027.
Slovakia’s central bank chief Peter Kazimir warned on November 2 that persistently high inflation could require the European Central Bank (ECB) to raise interest rates further, suggesting that markets may be underestimating the monetary tightening needed to bring inflation back to target.
Separately, the ECB announced on October 30 that it had selected two technology and telecommunications groups to provide network services for its digital euro project, marking another step toward testing the proposed central bank digital currency.
Kazimir Warns Inflation Could Require Further Rate Hikes
In a separate statement on November 2, Slovakia’s central bank chief Peter Kazimir warned that the ECB’s recent decision to hold interest rates steady should not be viewed as the end of monetary tightening. He cited persistent energy price pressures, rising food prices, and a weaker exchange rate that makes imports more expensive.
Kazimir said rising costs could eventually spread through the economy as businesses pass higher expenses on to consumers. He also warned that inflation expectations could shift before broader price pressures become visible in official data.
The ECB’s next policy decision is expected in December, when policymakers will have access to updated forecasts and additional economic information. Kazimir did not specify the number or size of any potential rate increases. However, he said markets might be underestimating how much further tightening would be needed to bring inflation back to the ECB’s target and keep it there.
For financial markets, the comments signal that interest-rate expectations could change if inflation remains persistent. However, the digital euro project and monetary policy decisions follow separate processes. Progress on the digital euro’s legislation and infrastructure should therefore be monitored independently of developments that could influence the ECB’s interest-rate decisions.
ECB Selects Two Digital Euro Network Groups
The ECB announced on October 30 that it had selected two groups to provide network services for the digital euro project.
The first group involves Nexi Payments and Deutsche Telekom Business Solutions. Their contract entered into force on September 28 and will initially provide connectivity for the digital euro pilot. The second group consists of Telefónica and Indra’s technology arm, Minsait. Its contract will start in May 2027.
The ECB’s official announcement states that both groups will connect participating payment service providers and national central banks to the digital euro service platform and enable communication between its components.
Both network providers will be ready as of 2029 to provide connectivity services for a potential digital euro issuance. Payment service providers will be able to choose either network to connect to the digital euro platform, subject to the ECB Governing Council’s decision on the project’s next phase.
Digital Euro Pilot Planned for 2027
The ECB intends to launch a 12-month pilot in the second half of 2027. Thirty-six selected payment service providers will participate in testing payments and assessing the system’s technical and operational capabilities.
However, the selection of network providers and the planned pilot do not constitute final approval for issuing the digital euro. The ECB has stated that a decision on issuance will only be made after the relevant European legislation is adopted and the Governing Council makes its decision. The pilot will help test the system and assess its readiness ahead of that decision.
The ECB is moving ahead with its digital euro preparations, while Kazimir’s warning puts the eurozone’s inflation outlook and potential rate hikes back in focus.

It was appropriate for the Bank of Japan to continue raising interest rates and adjust the degree of monetary accommodation in response to developments in the economy, prices, and financial conditions, according to its September meeting minutes.
Members agreed that the timing and pace of further adjustments should be determined by assessing the likelihood of achieving the central bank’s baseline economic and inflation outlook, while monitoring risks such as the impact of the situation in the Middle East, expanding AI-related demand, and forex movements.
They also stressed the growing importance of stabilising underlying CPI inflation around the 2% target to prevent an upward deviation that could hurt the economy.

articles.title: Bundesbank’s Nagel joins ECB chorus backing December rate hike - WKZO
articles.summary: Bundesbank’s Nagel joins ECB chorus backing December rate hike  WKZO
articles.full_text:
FRANKFURT, Nov 3 (Reuters) – Another European Central Bank rate hike in December seems almost inevitable, Bundesbank President Joachim Nagel said on Tuesday, joining an already long list of policymakers backing the move, which would be the bank’s third this year.
The ECB left its key deposit rate on hold at 2.5% last week on the premise that rapid inflation is not getting embedded but policymakers from different backgrounds and convictions have argued that the pause was likely temporary.
“From today’s perspective, an interest rate hike in December is very likely necessary,” Nagel, a crucial voice on the ECB’s Governing Council, said in a speech in Berlin. “There seems to be little alternative to an interest rate hike unless the inflation outlook improves significantly.”
While a December move is not fully priced in, financial investors see between two and three rate hikes over the coming year, as they expect inflation to hold above the 2% target for years to come.
Nagel argued that inflation was approaching the ECB’s ‘adverse’ scenario and price pressures would be higher than outlined in the bank’s September projections.
Bulgarian central bank chief Dimitar Radev, speaking earlier in the day, came to a similar conclusion.
“But the inflation outlook has deteriorated since September, and this must be reflected in our assessment of the appropriate monetary policy stance,” Radev said in a speech in Sofia. “The October pause was a decision to assess the evidence, not a conclusion that monetary policy tightening is over.”
The ECB sees inflation above 4% in the coming months, more than twice its target, falling back rapidly from early spring, when high year-earlier figures get knocked out of the time series.
While the ECB was ‘quite far’ from achieving its price stability mandate, Nagel also acknowledged that the inflation surge was primarily due to energy, over which the ECB has no control, and there was little evidence this increase was setting off second-round effects.
(Reporting by Balazs Koranyi; Editing by Xevi Fontdegloria)

articles.title: Democrats sweep U.S. Congress, triggering a rally in European bank stocks! Fiscal easing and cooling U.S. Treasury yields ignite market sentiment. - Moomoo
articles.summary: Democrats sweep U.S. Congress, triggering a rally in European bank stocks! Fiscal easing and cooling U.S. Treasury yields ignite market sentiment.  Moomoo
articles.full_text:
The Democrats' sweeping victory in the U.S. midterm elections has dispelled some of the uncertainty that had been weighing on equity markets, sending European shares higher as bank stocks led the gains. The STOXX 600 Banks Index surged as much as 4.5%.
The Zhitong Finance APP learned that the Democrats' sweep of the U.S. Congress has dampened market bets on further expansion of U.S. military spending, while boosting European bank stocks' expectations for an improved financing environment and credit outlook. The day's market dynamics also highlighted a rotation in expectations around Western policies: the Europe Stoxx 600 index rose nearly 1%, led by banking and clean energy sectors, while defense stocks lagged noticeably. Capital is being reallocated to different Democratic policy beneficiaries and directions amid the backdrop of the Democrats' congressional sweep.
Bank stocks led gains in European markets. The Democratic Party's sweeping victory in the U.S. midterm elections has dispelled some of the uncertainty that had weighed on equity markets in recent weeks, while falling bond yields have also provided a boost.
The Stoxx Europe 600 Banks index rose as much as 4.5%, on track for its best single-day gain since May. HSBC and Banco Santander, the largest stocks in the European banking sector, contributed the most to this round of index gains; Lion Finance Group and Ouhé International Bank led the advances, surging 5.9% and 6.4%, respectively. U.S. bank stocks also rose in pre-market trading.
Wednesday's rally marked a clear reversal in European bank stocks, which had plunged ahead of the election. The sector had pulled back from record highs hit in early September as U.S. and European bond yields surged recently, stoking market concerns about credit quality and default rates. Nevertheless, the sector is still up 11% year-to-date.
As shown in the chart above, ahead of the U.S. midterm elections, European bank stocks hovered near oversold pessimistic levels.
"Despite strong fundamentals, investors had already significantly reduced their exposure to bank stocks ahead of the midterm elections. As uncertainty has eased, we are now seeing a robust relief rally," said Ulrich Urban, Head of Multi-Asset Strategy and Research at Berenberg Bank. "This is a classic 'sell on the rumor, buy on the news' move."
As the results of the midterm elections were announced one after another, U.S. Treasury yields fell. Investors are betting that the new political environment will constrain the tax cuts led by the Trump administration and the U.S. government's massive fiscal spending plans. Bond yields in the United Kingdom, France, and Italy also declined.
"From a broader perspective, if financial conditions become significantly less restrictive and economic growth becomes more widespread, that would be positive for the international financial sector," said Geoff Yu, senior macro strategist at Bank of New York Mellon. "When people are reluctant to borrow and credit risk rises, a steep Treasury yield curve does not help banks improve their profitability."
With electoral pressures easing, European bank stocks are experiencing a "buy the rumor" rally.
At the heart of the sharp rebound in European bank stocks are the clear election outcome, the unwinding of prior deleveraging pressure, and falling bond yields, all of which have helped narrow the risk discount on bank shares. With Democrats sweeping the U.S. Congress, market bets on further increases in U.S. defense spending have weakened, while optimism among European banks about improving funding conditions and credit prospects has been boosted.
European bank stocks had earlier retreated from their early-September record highs, with the main pressure stemming from a sharp rise in U.S. and European government bond yields: higher funding costs began to threaten companies' debt-servicing capacity and loan demand, prompting investors to reassess risks related to non-performing loans and provisions.
A "blue Congress" refers to the Democratic Party controlling both the Senate and the House of Representatives. As mid-term election results indicated that Democrats would control both chambers, market expectations grew that Trump's efforts to introduce new tax cuts and spending plans would face greater constraints. Early European trading data from Reuters showed the yield on the U.S. 10-year Treasury note falling by about 2.1 basis points to 4.9291%, supporting a rebound in risk assets. Buying interest in bank stocks was driven by expectations that funding pressures might ease and the risk of earnings being eroded by credit losses would decline.
Pre-election portfolio adjustments further amplified the rebound. Berenberg Bank believes that banks' fundamentals remain strong, but investors had already significantly reduced their risk exposure, leading to a relief rally after the results were announced. Bloomberg Intelligence also noted a shift in capital toward European bank stocks, which had previously underperformed the broader market; during the same session, the defense sector came under pressure, indicating that the market is reallocating sectoral gains stemming from policy changes.
Why Falling Yields Are Good for Banks: Credit Quality Matters More Than Spread Widening
Bank profitability should not be assessed solely by whether lending rates rise. Higher interest rates can boost returns on some assets, but if borrowers cut back on borrowing, deposit and wholesale funding costs increase, and default losses mount, the margin gains may be offset.
When market concerns shift from "interest rates are not high enough" to "borrowers cannot withstand high benchmark borrowing costs," a decline in yields can actually benefit bank valuations. If improved financing conditions boost loan demand, ease debt-servicing pressures, and reduce expected credit losses, banks may sustain profitability through growth in business scale and improvements in asset quality.
This is also the crux of Bank of New York Mellon strategist Geoff Yu's view: a steep yield curve does not automatically mean banks are making more money; if companies are reluctant to borrow and credit risk rises, the curve's advantages will be hard to realize. Investors would prefer to see economic growth spread across more sectors, financing activity pick up, and bank profits no longer overly reliant on interest rates or the yield curve continuing to steepen.
Some banks already have the operational foundation to support valuation recovery. HSBC's third-quarter profit before tax, on a constant-currency basis and excluding major items, rose 10% year over year; as of end-September, Santander's Common Equity Tier 1 capital ratio stood at 12.7%, above the minimum requirement of 9.86%. Profit growth and capital buffers provide support for banks to absorb potential losses and sustain credit supply. The sustainability of the banking sector's rebound will depend more on whether easing funding pressures translate into steady loan growth, stable credit costs, and consistent shareholder returns, rather than on day-to-day fluctuations in yields.

articles.title: Fed holds interest rates steady as inflation hits 3-year high - ABC News - Breaking News, Latest News and Videos
articles.summary: Fed holds interest rates steady as inflation hits 3-year high  ABC News - Breaking News, Latest News and Videos

source_detail.name: ABC News - Breaking News, Latest News and Videos

articles.full_text:
Futures markets overwhelmingly expected the Fed to keep rates unchanged.
The Federal Reserve held interest rates steady on Wednesday as the economy weathers its highest inflation in three years.
The announcement marked the first decision on interest rates rates since Trump nominee Kevin Warsh took the helm as Fed chair.
Speaking at a press conference, Warsh voiced a commitment to bring inflation down to the Fed's desired level of 2%. The annual pace of price increases currently registers at more than twice that target rate.
"Persistently high prices are a burden for the American people," Warsh told reporters in Washington, D.C. "This committee will deliver price stability."
All 12 members of the FOMC voted to hold interest rates steady, meaning Warsh and his predecessor, former Fed Chair Jerome Powell, agreed on the rate decision.
Nine members indicated they expect to raise interest rates by the end of the year, marking a significant change in sentiment from a previous projection issued three months earlier.
The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC), a 12-member policymaking body at the Fed, issued a statement describing inflation as "elevated."
The current level of inflation in part reflects "supply shocks that have driven price increases in certain sectors, including energy," the FOMC said.
The policy move also arrived at a moment of flux for the nation’s economy, just days after an agreement between the United States and Iran offered hope for some price relief.
The U.S.-Iran accord, set to be formally signed on Friday, came as gasoline prices fell below $4 a gallon for the first time since March. Still, fuel costs stand well above pre-war levels, and an array of grocery prices remain elevated.
In recent weeks, odds have risen for a potential interest rate hike by the end of 2026, according to the CME FedWatch Tool, which grants a roughly four in 10 chance of a quarter-point increase in December.
The shift in expectations came after a stronger-than-expected jobs report earlier this month showed robust hiring in May. In theory, a resilient labor market could afford central bankers leeway to raise interest rates in an effort to dial back inflation, since elevated borrowing costs risk a hiring slowdown.
Inflation jumped for a third consecutive month as the Iran war continued to drive up prices in May, surpassing 4% for the first time in three years
The Middle East conflict prompted the Iranian closure of the Strait of Hormuz, a maritime trading route that facilitates the transport of about one-fifth of global oil supply. The standoff triggered one of the largest oil shocks ever recorded, sending gasoline prices surging.
On Monday, President Donald Trump announced a U.S.-Iran deal that included plans to reopen the strait. Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi confirmed the deal had been finalized and said it would be signed in Switzerland on Friday. Oil prices fell to their lowest level since March.
The benchmark rate stands at a level between 3.5% and 3.75%. That figure marks a significant drop from a recent peak attained in 2023, but borrowing costs remain well above a 0% rate established at the outset of the COVID-19 pandemic.
The rate decision is the first major policy move overseen by Warsh. During his term as a Fed governor in the late 2000s and early 2010s, Warsh gained a reputation as an interest-rate "hawk," meaning he generally preferred higher interest rates as a means of ensuring low and stable inflation.
Last year, Warsh voiced support for lower interest rates. At his Senate confirmation hearing in April, Warsh emphasized the threat posed by elevated inflation.
"When inflation surges -- as it has done in recent years -- grievous harm is done to our citizens, especially to the least well-off," Warsh said.
Bucking typical norms, Powell casted a vote on interest rates as a member of the Fed's policymaking board.
Powell said he would stay on at the central bank's board of governors after his term as chair expired as an investigation into the Fed's office renovation continues.
The Department of Justice moved to drop a criminal probe into Powell in April, calling on the Fed's inspector general to carry out the investigation into cost overruns tied to the renovation. Powell will remain on the Fed's board for an indeterminate length of time, he said last month.
The criminal investigation into Powell focused on alleged false testimony to Congress about an office renovation. Powell, who was appointed by Trump in 2017, has rebuked the probe as a politically motivated effort to influence interest-rate policy. Trump denied any involvement in the criminal investigation.

articles.title: Analysis: Lula’s advisers warn of risks from aggressive rate cuts - Valor International
articles.summary: Analysis: Lula’s advisers warn of risks from aggressive rate cuts  Valor International
articles.full_text:
Analysis: Lula’s advisers warn of risks from aggressive rate cuts
André Lara Resende, a Real Plan architect whose proposals have been presented to Brazil’s president, advocates sharp Selic reduction and use of foreign reserves to curb currency depreciation
Atualizado
Proposals by economist André Lara Resende, which have been presented to President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva as a possible economic agenda for his fourth term, are raising concerns within the government's economic team. Officials fear the ideas could destabilize financial markets even if they are ultimately rejected.
Lara Resende, considered one of the architects of Brazil's Real Plan, has advocated lowering the benchmark Selic interest rate to 7.5% a year over 12 months. The goal is to reduce the government's borrowing costs and bring public finances into balance without the pain of spending cuts or tax increases.
In internal government discussions, economic officials have warned that an interest rate reduction perceived by investors as artificial would prompt a rush into foreign currencies and an exodus from government bonds.
In an article published on the newsletter platform Substack, Lara Resende acknowledges the possibility of such short-term reactions but argues that the Central Bank should use its international reserves to contain a surge in the dollar.
Members of the economic team counter that Brazil's $372.6 billion in foreign reserves could be depleted rapidly if the monetary authority attempted to resist a wave of capital flight.
Daily financial transactions involving the dollar and the real across different markets currently total roughly $80 billion. If investors suspect the Central Bank is defending a ceiling for the dollar, bets against the Brazilian currency could multiply quickly.
China's experience in 2015 offers a particularly telling example of what can happen when a central bank tries to defend its currency during a shift in economic policy. At the time, China held $4 trillion in reserves but spent $1 trillion in a relatively short period, with limited success in containing speculative pressure.
Government economists warn that adopting Lara Resende's approach could quickly strip Brazil of one of its most important economic safeguards: the international reserves accumulated during Lula's first two terms.
Those reserves cannot prevent the real from depreciating when the exchange rate moves toward a new equilibrium, but they have proved valuable in cushioning external shocks, including during the global financial crisis.
Depleting them could leave Brazil in a position closer to Argentina's, dependent on International Monetary Fund (IMF) rescue programs with far more stringent economic conditions to weather external crises.
Government debt risks
Lara Resende argues that Brazil has an advantage because a large share of its public debt is indexed to the Selic rate. Under his proposal, lowering the benchmark would immediately reduce the interest paid by the government. Over time, he believes, fixed-rate debt would be replaced by floating-rate securities.
Government economists, however, caution that the transition could prove traumatic.
Floating-rate government securities, known as Financial Treasury Bills (LFTs), have been trading at discounts for some time. This means investors demand an additional premium to hold them because of credit risk.
A shift in the economic policy regime could make investors increasingly reluctant to buy these securities.
A similar episode occurred during the 2002 presidential election, when uncertainty over Lula's economic program for his first term prompted investors to shun LFTs. The selloff was intensified by the mark-to-market valuation mechanism for the securities that the Central Bank had introduced at the time.
When investors turn away from LFTs, the Treasury may be forced to repurchase its debt to prevent the premiums demanded by the market from widening further.
Economic officials warn that the National Treasury's liquidity buffer, currently slightly below R$1 trillion, would be insufficient to absorb an investor exodus from a public debt stock exceeding R$11 trillion.
Under those circumstances, the only remaining option would be for the Central Bank to create money and transfer resources to the Treasury.
Such monetary financing would represent a step toward hyperinflation, with government expenditure effectively funded by the Central Bank's printing press.
Market uncertainty
Over the weekend, Finance Minister Dario Durigan said no meeting had been scheduled between Lara Resende and Lula and that the economist's proposals were not under consideration.
Whether Durigan's statements will reassure investors when markets reopen after the holiday on Nov. 2 remains unclear.
Until now, investors had been uncertain about the direction of Lula's fourth administration, but the perceived options appeared relatively limited.
One possibility was a more forceful fiscal adjustment capable of restoring confidence in government finances. The other was a continuation of the gradual approach adopted during Lula's previous term, widely regarded as slow and marked by reversals and compromises designed to accommodate the president's electoral interests.
Reports that Lara Resende's ideas have been brought to Lula's attention introduce a much more disruptive possibility: a radical break with the government's existing economic policy direction.
Durigan told Valor that several economists had contacted him and Brazilian Development Bank (BNDES) President Aloizio Mercadante to offer their views and make themselves available for discussions.
As Valor reported last week, a behind-the-scenes struggle is underway over the economic agenda for Lula's fourth term.
On one side, the current economic team argues that continuing fiscal adjustments offers the safest path forward.
On the other, a group of economists with longstanding ties to the Workers' Party (PT), including Mercadante and former Finance Minister Guido Mantega, opposes fiscal tightening, which they view as a "betrayal of campaign promises."
The outcome of that dispute remains uncertain.
But the lack of clarity has already taken a substantial toll on financial markets. Last week, the real weakened sharply against the dollar, while inflation expectations embedded in government bond prices came under intense upward pressure, a development likely to spill over into broader market inflation forecasts.
These movements increase the government's interest expenses and make the fiscal adjustment needed to contain the rapid growth of public debt even more painful.
Political resistance
Developmentalist economists advising Lula argue that the president should not give in to what they consider market blackmail.
Their position is that Brazil's financial markets are dominated by a liberal economic worldview aligned with defeated presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro, and that investors are trying to force the democratically elected president to abandon his social agenda.
Yet financial market pressure on governments is hardly unique to Brazil.
In France, government bond yields have reached their highest levels in 24 years amid concerns about the country's fragile public finances.
In the United Kingdom, former Prime Minister Liz Truss saw her leadership brought to an abrupt end in 2022 after investors rejected her mini-budget, driving interest rates to historic highs.
The United States is also facing pressure in its bond market, although economists disagree on whether the driving factors are fiscal concerns, a wave of borrowing by artificial intelligence companies or monetary policy pursued by the Federal Reserve.
The U.S. enjoys greater protection because it issues the world's principal reserve currency.
For an emerging economy such as Brazil, however, investors tend to have less patience than they do with advanced economies, and bouts of market panic can be far more severe.
The uncertainty fueled by Lula in the days following his reelection could therefore have tangible consequences for the real economy, even if the government ultimately rejects proposals viewed by investors as radical and opts instead for fiscal adjustment.

articles.title: US stocks soaring, Dow up 1,500 points, Brent oil price drops below $95 per barrel - Las Vegas Review-Journal
articles.summary: US stocks soaring, Dow up 1,500 points, Brent oil price drops below $95 per barrel  Las Vegas Review-Journal
articles.full_text:
NEW YORK— U.S. stocks are soaring Wednesday after President Donald Trump’s party lost its sole control of Washington in the midterm elections.
Stocks generally do well in the months following any midterm U.S. election, regardless of who wins, and the S&P 500 jumped 1.8%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 1,501 points, or 2.9%, as of 1:11 p.m. Eastern time, and the Nasdaq composite was 2.1% higher.
Stocks of solar-power companies, dollar stores and hospital owners helped lead the way as Wall Street tried to sort the winners from losers following the widespread losses for Republicans. Investors, meanwhile, see risks ahead for Trump’s social-media company, the artificial-intelligence industry and businesses owned by Elon Musk, who donated heavily to Republicans.
The price for a barrel of Brent crude oil fell below $100 for the first time in nearly a month. Vice President JD Vance blamed the war with Iran, which caused a spike in oil prices, for Republicans’ midterm losses.
Strategists along Wall Street had been urging investors not to get swept up in the election because it may not matter much for the broad market in the long term. Prices for stocks depend more on where profits for companies and interest rates are heading than on who controls what in Washington.
“Earnings trump elections,” according to Brian Jacobsen, chief economic strategist at Annex Wealth Management.
Still, Wall Street may have gotten a preferred political scenario as Democrats are set to take control of both the Senate and the House of Representatives. Wall Street generally prefers split control of Washington because it lessens the risk of transformative changes to the economy.
Much remains impossible to predict, of course, and Trump retains executive authority over key areas such as defense, foreign policy and in some instances trade.
A downbeat forecast could be that “Trump is not now a lame duck, but an angry duck” who might restart tensions over tariffs and NATO allies’ levels of military spending, said Carsten Brzeski, global chief of macro at ING Bank.
An optimistic view, Brzeski said, is that Trump becomes “a tame duck … that he will slow down any disruptive efforts and that he will put more focus on trying to win the Nobel Peace Prize by ending the two big wars without big disruption, and on trade, nothing happens but a few words.”
Here’s a look at some of the moves rippling through financial markets:
Trump Media and Tesla are down
Trump’s social-media company, Trump Media & Technology Group, was one of the market’s bigger losers, down 15.9%.
Since briefly touching a peak of $175 five years ago, it’s dropped toward $5. Its main business is Truth Social, which is most well known for Trump’s postings on the platform.
Elon Musk’s businesses also struggled. Tesla fell 2%, and SpaceX sank 3.4%. Musk, a former top Trump adviser, is among the possible targets for investigations by a Democratic-controlled Congress.
AI companies in general are under pressure
Trump has been a big backer of the AI industry, and Democratic victories across the country could mean more regulation or restrictions. Concerns have grown across political parties about AI in general.
Investors see Democratic wins in Texas in particular as possibly slowing the build out of further AI data centers. AI-related stocks came into Election Day already under pressure because of worries their prices had shot too high.
Nvidia, the chip company that quickly became the poster child of the frenzy around AI-related stocks, sank 1.4% and was the heaviest weight on the S&P 500. CoreWeave, a company that rents out access to AI chips to customers over the cloud, dropped 9.1%
Advanced Micro Devices, another chip giant, held up better. It added 0.5% after reporting much stronger profit for the latest quarter than analysts expected.
Companies that have been spending heavily on AI chips also did better. Alphabet rose 4.4%, for example, after it tumbled more than 12% Thursday to its worst loss ever on worries that it was spending too much on AI investments.
Defense stocks are down
A Democratic-led Congress could push Trump to pull back on the war with Iran.
That helped send down stocks of companies that make weapons and other equipment for the U.S. military, including drops of 6.9% for Lockheed Martin, 4.4% for Northrop Grumman and 2.3% for General Dynamics.
Green power companies are up, and oil prices are down
Democratic control of Congress could light the way for companies in the solar and wind industries. First Solar jumped 6.4%, and Enphase Energy climbed 6.2%.
Stocks of big oil companies, meanwhile, sank. ExxonMobil fell 5.3%, and ConocoPhillips dropped 5.9%. They had been rallying for much of the year after Trump and Israel began the war with Iran, which sent crude prices much higher.
The price for a barrel of Brent crude, the international standard, plunged 8.8% Wednesday to $94.51.
The price for the most actively traded contract in the Brent market has been veering between roughly $70 and $120 per barrel since just before the war with Iran began.
Healthcare stocks and dollar stores also rallied
A Democratic-led Congress could try to reverse some of the cuts to federal healthcare and food assistance that Republicans approved during the summer in their “One Big Beautiful Bill Act.”
That helped stocks climb across the healthcare industry, including a rise of 10.6% for HCA Healthcare, which runs hospitals and ambulatory sites.
Retailers also benefited on hopes that Democrats may push policies to help Americans struggling to keep up with the fast-rising cost of living. Dollar Tree, which focuses in particular on lower-income Americans, had one of the market’s bigger leaps and rose 8.9%.
Bond yields are down
In the bond market, Treasury yields eased. That could be a signal investors see less risk of Washington piling even more debt onto its already big mountain with the coming end to one-party control.
Treasury yields had surged through the summer and reached their highest levels in decades because of worries about the U.S. government’s big debt, along with higher inflation and other concerns. A Congress controlled by Democrats could provide a check against more spending and cuts to taxes that would widen Washington’s deficit.
The yield on the 10-year Treasury fell to 4.91% from 4.95% late Tuesday.
Stocks jump in much of the world
Indexes climbed across most of the world. Stocks leaped 2% in Paris, 2.2% in Shanghai and 1.8% in London. Japan’s Nikkei 225 was an outlier and fell 1.4%.
———
AP Writer Elaine Lai contributed to this report from Hong Kong, and McHugh contributed from Frankfurt, Germany.

articles.title: WTI Crude Climbs Toward $96 on US-Iran Diplomatic Risks - TradingPedia
articles.summary: WTI Crude Climbs Toward $96 on US-Iran Diplomatic Risks  TradingPedia
articles.full_text:
Key Moments
- WTI trades near $96.10 per barrel in Asian dealings on Wednesday, extending a two-day rebound.
- The US has signaled no immediate plan to strike Iran, while Israel has suggested an attack could come this week.
- Despite the latest bounce, WTI remains down about 6% for the week amid optimism over diplomacy and improving Middle East exports.
WTI Rebounds as Traders Track US-Iran Negotiations
West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude oil is advancing for a second straight session, changing hands around $96.10 per barrel during Asian trading on Wednesday. The benchmark is recovering after a steep slide of nearly 7% earlier in the week, as investors reassess the outlook for Middle East supply and the trajectory of peace efforts between the United States and Iran.
Oil prices are finding support as markets digest conflicting signals. While diplomatic activity has intensified, lingering uncertainty over the outcome of talks and the potential for further military action is keeping volatility elevated.
Diplomatic Efforts Intensify, But Tehran Criticizes US Response
A spokesperson for Qatar’s Foreign Ministry said that both Washington and Tehran are reviewing fresh proposals from mediators intended to narrow their differences. These initiatives are aimed at advancing ongoing peace discussions.
However, Iran’s national security chief, in a social media post, described Washington’s current reply to the proposals as unsatisfactory, underscoring the fragility of the negotiations and tempering optimism in the market.
US Signals Caution on Military Action As Israel Hints at Possible Strike
According to the Financial Times, US President Donald Trump indicated that the United States has no immediate intention to launch strikes against Iran and suggested the US is “getting what it wants.” He stated that the US is prepared to act if circumstances require it but noted there may ultimately be no need to do so, even as Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has hinted at a potential attack later this week.
Earlier this week, the US carried out what it described as defensive strikes against Iran, focusing on surface-to-air missile systems that had been used against American assets. The limited and targeted nature of these actions has been interpreted as a sign that a broader, large-scale military campaign is not imminent.
Weekly Performance: WTI Still Lower Despite Short-Term Bounce
Despite the latest uptick, the US crude benchmark remains lower by roughly 6% so far this week. The recent pullback has been driven in part by growing hopes for a diplomatic breakthrough in US-Iran relations, coupled with indications that crude exports from the Middle East are recovering.
| Metric | Detail | 
|---|---|
| Current WTI level | Around $96.10 per barrel (Asian session, Wednesday) | 
| Recent weekly move | Down about 6% so far this week | 
| Earlier weekly decline | Nearly 7% drop on easing Middle East supply fears | 
WTI Oil: Key Characteristics and Market Role
WTI Oil is a grade of crude oil traded on international markets. The acronym WTI stands for West Texas Intermediate, one of three primary global oil grades alongside Brent and Dubai Crude. It is described as “light” due to its relatively low gravity and “sweet” because of its relatively low sulfur content. These properties make it a high-quality crude that is relatively straightforward to refine.
WTI is produced in the United States and is distributed through the Cushing hub, widely known as “The Pipeline Crossroads of the World.” It serves as a key benchmark for the global oil market, and the WTI price is frequently cited across financial media and energy markets.
Fundamental Drivers of WTI Pricing
The price of WTI Oil is primarily shaped by supply and demand dynamics. Periods of stronger global economic growth can bolster demand for crude, while weaker growth can have the opposite effect.
Other major influences include:
- Political instability, wars, and sanctions that can disrupt supply and affect pricing.
- Decisions by OPEC, which comprises major oil-producing nations that coordinate on production quotas.
- The value of the US dollar, since oil is mostly transacted in dollars; a weaker dollar can make oil relatively cheaper for holders of other currencies, and a stronger dollar can make it more expensive.
Impact of Inventory Data on WTI
Weekly inventory statistics published by the American Petroleum Institute (API) and the Energy Information Agency (EIA) are closely watched indicators for WTI pricing. These reports provide insight into evolving supply-demand balances.
Key points on inventory data:
- A decline in inventories can signal stronger demand or tighter supply, which may support higher prices.
- An increase in inventories can indicate looser market conditions, which may weigh on prices.
- API typically releases its figures every Tuesday, followed by the EIA report the next day.
- The two data sets are often aligned, with results falling within 1% of each other 75% of the time.
- EIA data is generally viewed as more reliable because it is produced by a government agency.
OPEC and Its Influence on WTI
OPEC (Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries) is an alliance of 12 oil-producing states that collectively determine production quotas for members at meetings held twice a year. These decisions can significantly influence WTI pricing.
When OPEC announces lower production quotas, the resulting reduction in supply can push oil prices higher. Conversely, an increase in production quotas can add supply and pressure prices lower.
The broader grouping known as OPEC+ includes an additional ten non-OPEC producers, with Russia being the most prominent among them. Decisions by OPEC+ also play an important role in shaping expectations and pricing in the WTI market.

articles.title: Macroeconomic Outlook: How Federal Reserve Interest Rate Expectations and Big Tech Earnings Drive Crypto Risk Appetite - KuCoin
articles.summary: Macroeconomic Outlook: How Federal Reserve Interest Rate Expectations and Big Tech Earnings Drive Crypto Risk Appetite  KuCoin
articles.full_text:
Introduction
The macro environment dictates digital asset valuations, with crypto assets maintaining a high correlation to equity indices during periods of monetary policy shifts. According to the Federal Reserve's economic projections, ongoing adjustments to the federal funds target range directly influence institutional liquidity allocation, establishing a direct pipeline between traditional financial markets and cryptocurrency volatility. Understanding how macroeconomic policy decisions and corporate earnings performance intersect is essential for navigating market cycles.
Decoding Federal Reserve Interest Rate Policy and Crypto Liquidity
Federal Reserve interest rate decisions dictate global market liquidity, with lower rates expanding the money supply and driving capital into high-beta assets like cryptocurrencies. According to data from Trading Economics, the Federal Reserve maintained the federal funds target range at 3.75%–4.00%, following a 25 basis point rate increase that marked a persistent tightening posture. When borrowing costs remain elevated, institutional investors reallocate capital away from speculative digital assets toward fixed-income yields.
The primary transmission channel between central bank policy and crypto valuations is systemic liquidity. According to macroeconomic analyses published by S&P Global, periods of monetary contraction and balance sheet reduction historically coincide with compressed valuations across major digital assets. Conversely, anticipation of monetary easing lowers the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding assets, creating favorable conditions for sustained market expansions. Traders must continuously monitor FOMC statements and core inflation metrics to anticipate near-term liquidity shocks.
The Big Tech Earnings Nexus and Market Risk Appetite
Big Tech earnings performance functions as an immediate macro catalyst for cryptocurrency prices, with rolling correlations exceeding 0.60 between mega-cap equities and digital tokens. According to market analyses from eToro, combined trailing annual free cash flow for major technology conglomerates has faced scrutiny due to aggressive capital expenditures in artificial intelligence infrastructure and data centers. Because institutional asset managers group high-growth tech stocks and cryptocurrencies into the same risk-on asset class, earnings reports from industry leaders dictate cross-market sentiment.
When technology giants report earnings beats and robust forward guidance, systemic risk appetite expands, prompting capital inflows into spot exchange-traded funds and derivatives markets. Conversely, margin contraction or heavy capital expenditure guidance triggers immediate equity drawdowns, spilling over into accelerated crypto liquidations. According to on-chain derivatives data tracked across major institutional platforms, sudden risk-off moves in equities frequently trigger multi-million dollar redemptions in crypto ETFs, proving that digital assets remain highly sensitive to broader equity sentiment.
Institutional Plumbing: ETF Flows and Derivative Positioning
Institutional capital flows through regulated spot ETFs and derivatives exchanges create the modern bridge between macroeconomic data releases and digital asset price action. According to aggregated exchange data, single-day ETF redemptions spike during broader equity market corrections, demonstrating that institutional participants manage cross-asset risk uniformly. This institutionalization has fundamentally altered market mechanics, ensuring that macro shocks are priced into crypto order books faster than in previous market cycles.
Derivative market positioning reflects this heightened sensitivity, with options markets consistently pricing in elevated volatility premiums ahead of major FOMC meetings and corporate earnings announcements. Traders monitor funding rates, open interest shifts, and put-to-call skew ratios to evaluate whether leverage is overextended. When macroeconomic uncertainty climbs, negative skews indicate that institutional participants are actively bidding for downside protection, signaling a defensive stance across both equity and crypto portfolios.
Persistent inflation prints complicate monetary policy trajectories, forcing central banks to maintain restrictive stances that challenge crypto market momentum. According to the Federal Reserve Bank of New York’s Survey of Consumer Expectations, medium-term inflation expectations remain elevated, signaling that price pressures are sticky across core consumer sectors. Higher inflation prints diminish the likelihood of aggressive rate cuts, directly undermining the speculative expansion thesis for digital assets.
Concurrently, labor market resilience dictates the Federal Reserve’s timeline for policy pivots. A robust labor market gives central bankers the leeway to keep interest rates restrictive without triggering immediate economic contraction, keeping pressure on risk-on sectors. Investors evaluating macro risk must analyze employment reports alongside consumer price indices, as labor stability directly dictates how long monetary policy will remain a headwind for the cryptocurrency ecosystem.
Strategic Positioning Amid Macroeconomic Shifts
Navigating macro-driven markets requires disciplined risk management, strict adherence to technical support zones, and constant evaluation of cross-asset correlations. Because digital assets behave as high-beta extensions of global liquidity, portfolio construction must account for potential drawdowns triggered by traditional financial market corrections. Utilizing decentralized options, maintaining appropriate cash reserves, and monitoring institutional fund flows allow participants to protect capital during periods of heightened macroeconomic transition.
Long-term market resilience depends on the maturation of blockchain utility independent of central bank liquidity cycles, but short-term price discovery remains tethered to macro fundamentals. Traders who align their strategies with upcoming macroeconomic calendar events—such as FOMC rate decisions, Consumer Price Index releases, and mega-cap tech earnings disclosures—are better positioned to capitalize on volatility spikes. Success in modern crypto trading requires viewing blockchain assets not in isolation, but as an integral component of the global macroeconomic risk spectrum.
FAQs
How do changes in the US M2 money supply impact cryptocurrency valuations?
Changes in the M2 money supply directly alter the volume of fiat liquidity available for speculative investment. According to historical market studies by S&P Global, expansions in M2 resulting from quantitative easing or lower interest rates consistently precede major cryptocurrency bull runs, while monetary contraction restricts capital inflows and drives market corrections.
Why do institutional investors trade crypto and Big Tech stocks in tandem?
Institutional portfolio managers classify both high-growth technology equities and digital assets as high-beta, risk-on growth instruments. When macroeconomic conditions tighten or institutional risk models signal vulnerability, automated risk-management systems reduce exposure across both asset classes simultaneously.
What role do spot ETFs play in linking macro data to crypto prices?
Regulated spot ETFs provide institutional capital with direct access to digital assets, establishing automated channels for traditional finance capital allocation. Consequently, macro-driven outflows from traditional equity funds frequently trigger proportional redemptions in crypto ETFs, accelerating the transmission of macroeconomic shocks to blockchain markets.
How do producer and consumer price indices affect Federal Reserve policy decisions?
Producer and consumer price indices measure inflationary pressures across goods, services, and raw materials within the broader economy. When these indices print above consensus forecasts, the Federal Reserve responds by maintaining restrictive interest rates or signaling further policy tightening to combat inflation, which dampens risk appetite for digital assets.
Why are options volatility premiums important around earnings and FOMC releases?
Options volatility premiums quantify the degree of expected price movement priced in by institutional derivatives traders ahead of major high-impact events. Elevated volatility premiums indicate acute market uncertainty, allowing sophisticated traders to identify potential mispricings and manage directional risk effectively.

articles.full_text:
Key Moments
- The People’s Bank of China (PBOC) set the USD/CNY central parity rate at 6.7150 for Tuesday’s session.
- The new fixing compared with the previous day’s reference rate of 6.7146.
- The official midpoint diverged from a 6.6489 estimate cited by Reuters.
Latest USD/CNY Central Parity Setting
The People’s Bank of China (PBOC) set the central parity rate for USD/CNY at 6.7150 for the upcoming Tuesday trading session. This official midpoint was slightly higher than the prior day’s fixing level of 6.7146 and differed from a 6.6489 estimate reported by Reuters.
| Reference | USD/CNY Level | 
|---|---|
| Current PBOC fixing (Tuesday) | 6.7150 | 
| Previous day’s fixing | 6.7146 | 
| Reuters estimate | 6.6489 | 
Mandate and Role of the People’s Bank of China
The primary monetary policy objectives of the People’s Bank of China (PBoC) are to safeguard price stability, including exchange rate stability, and promote economic growth. China’s central bank also aims to implement financial reforms, such as opening and developing the financial market.
Governance and Ownership Structure
The PBoC is owned by the state of the People’s Republic of China (PRC), so it is not considered an autonomous institution. The Chinese Communist Party (CCP) Committee Secretary, nominated by the Chairman of the State Council, has a key influence on the PBoC’s management and direction, not the governor. However, Mr. Pan Gongsheng currently holds both of these posts.
Policy Toolkit and Key Interest Rate Benchmarks
Unlike the Western economies, the PBoC uses a broader set of monetary policy instruments to achieve its objectives. The primary tools include a seven-day Reverse Repo Rate (RRR), Medium-term Lending Facility (MLF), foreign exchange interventions and Reserve Requirement Ratio (RRR). However, The Loan Prime Rate (LPR) is China’s benchmark interest rate. Changes to the LPR directly influence the rates that need to be paid in the market for loans and mortgages and the interest paid on savings. By changing the LPR, China’s central bank can also influence the exchange rates of the Chinese Renminbi.
Private Banking Landscape in China
Yes, China has 19 private banks – a small fraction of the financial system. The largest private banks are digital lenders WeBank and MYbank, which are backed by tech giants Tencent and Ant Group, per The Straits Times. In 2014, China allowed domestic lenders fully capitalized by private funds to operate in the state-dominated financial sector.

iShares Broad USD High Yield Corporate Bond ETF (CBOEBZX:USHY) follows a US dollar high-yield corporate bond benchmark. The portfolio focuses on borrowers below the investment-grade category, where repayment capacity and refinancing access Warrant particular attention. Its broad mandate spreads exposure among issuers, while the Credit cycle can still affect many of those issuers together.
Investment approach and market coverage
iShares Broad USD High Yield Corporate Bond ETF (CBOEBZX:USHY) uses an index-tracking mandate. The stated benchmark is ICE BofA US High Yield Constrained Index. The benchmark defines the eligible Investment universe, and its membership and weights shape the portfolio. An index objective does not mean the fund and benchmark will match exactly. Expenses, transactions, cash balances and implementation decisions can create differences. The scope of the mandate matters when comparing this exposure with an existing portfolio, because funds with similar names may cover different securities or market segments.
Holdings and underlying exposure
In the official holdings file dated 3 November 2026, selected leading individual bond positions were 1261229 Bc Ltd 144A maturing 15 April 2032 at 0.49%; Echostar Corp maturing 30 November 2029 at 0.39%; Meridian Arc Holdco Llc 144A maturing 30 April 2031 at 0.36%; Paramount Skydance Corp 144A maturing 15 October 2031 at 0.33%; Softbank Group Corp 144A maturing 1 April 2032 at 0.32%. These figures are security-level portfolio weights; separate securities from the same issuer may appear in other rows. Holdings and weights can change.
Aggregating the reported bond rows by the issuer file’s sector labels gives Corporates at approximately 99.21%, Government Related at approximately 0.26%, Other at approximately 0.00%. These are calculated sums of rounded security weights, rather than a separate issuer-published allocation table. Cash, Derivatives and other asset classes are excluded from these sector sums. The composition helps explain which economic exposures accompany the stated mandate.
Fees distributions and share pricing
iShares Broad USD High Yield Corporate Bond ETF (CBOEBZX:USHY) has a listed gross annual expense ratio of 0.08% and net annual expense ratio of 0.08%. At the net rate, USD 10,000 held at a constant value for a full year would imply approximately USD 8.00 in annual fund expenses. This is an illustrative fee calculation, excluding changes in value, brokerage costs and bid-ask spreads. Expenses are reflected within the product rather than quoted as a promised investment outcome.
The stated distribution frequency is monthly. The schedule describes how often distributions are expected, while payment amounts depend on income and other applicable fund circumstances. A distribution is distinct from Capital appreciation and does not establish a fixed future payment. Shareholders also need to consider their own tax treatment, including any treatment of distributions or gains on sale.
iShares reported net asset value of USD 35.67 per share as at 4 November 2026. NAV measures the underlying net asset value allocated to a share; it is not an exchange closing-price quotation. Shares trade on Cboe BZX, where the transaction price can differ from NAV and where the bid-ask spread adds to the cost of entering or exiting a position.
Repayment risk and the credit cycle
High-yield borrowers can be particularly vulnerable to weaker earnings, tighter lending conditions and difficulties refinancing debt. Defaults or restructurings may lead to losses, and stressed markets can make bonds harder to trade. Diversifying across issuers reduces dependence on one borrower but does not neutralize a broad credit downturn. An income-oriented corporate bond allocation can therefore experience material capital Volatility alongside its distributions.
Key Insights
iShares Broad USD High Yield Corporate Bond ETF (CBOEBZX:USHY) is defined by its benchmark and eligible investment universe. Its holdings explain the actual exposure, while the fee schedule and distribution arrangements explain important ownership mechanics. These features need to be considered together: broad coverage, a particular style or a specified Maturity band each changes the risks a Shareholder takes. The investment objective remains a target, and the value of the shares can decline.

articles.summary: Housing stocks rally following midterm elections, Treasury yields dip lower  Yahoo FinanceHere’s where Trump’s housing agenda stands before midterms  CNNHere’s What Democrats Taking Back the House and Senate Could Mean for Housing Stocks Like Home Depot and Lowe’s  Yahoo FinanceThe housing ballot initiatives to watch in the 2026 midterm elections  Reason MagazineWhy The Blue Wave Won’t Make a Big Splash in the Housing Market  Mansion Global
articles.full_text:
Homebuilders and housing supplier stocks jumped on Wednesday in the wake of the midterm elections.
Lennar (LEN) was up more than 8%, and D.R. Horton (DHI) and PulteGroup (PHM) also rose around 8% in midday trading.
Housing suppliers also rode the wave. Home Depot (HD) soared more than 17% before paring gains to 5%. Lowe's (LOW) jumped 15% and is now up 7%.
The 10-year Treasury yield (^TNX), the benchmark for mortgage rates, moved slightly lower.
The Democrats' sweep in Congress is fueling anticipation of new action in Washington on housing affordability, a prominent issue during the midterm campaign, and the potential for lower mortgage rates in a shifting macroeconomic environment.
The housing market is mired in an unyielding rut, hemmed in by high home prices and high mortgage rates. Homebuyers, especially younger, first-time buyers, are struggling to break into the market.
Read more: How to get the lowest mortgage rates right now
Despite the deadlock, Congress passed the first major piece of housing legislation in decades this year, a sprawling bill that addresses housing affordability by encouraging more homebuilding, expanding financing options, providing grants for local governments that ease zoning restrictions and expand the housing supply, and streamlining environmental review processes, among other provisions.
With Democrats assuming power and promising to address Americans' cost-of-living concerns, more legislative action could materialize — particularly on the demand side.
TD Cowen wrote in a post-election note that Rep. Maxine Waters of California, who could become chair of the House Financial Services Committee, plans to focus on housing, including down payment help and funds to renovate public housing. The analysts added, however, that they "remain dubious it will become law."
Analysts for UBS cited additional affordable housing grant funding and tax benefits for first-time homebuyers and multifamily housing developers as potential areas for congressional action. 
Molly Moorhead is economics editor for Yahoo Finance.

articles.title: ‘The new frontier of finance is built in the United States of America’ - Financial Times
articles.summary: ‘The new frontier of finance is built in the United States of America’  Financial TimesCboe, Citadel Securities-backed group sues US regulator over single-stock perpetual futures  ReutersTrading on US Stock Perpetuals Contracts Is Approved by CFTC  Bloomberg.comU.S. clears path for first regulated equity perpetual futures  MarketWatchCapital Markets Alliance Files Suit Challenging CFTC Approval of Single-Stock Perpetual Derivatives  Business Wire
articles.full_text:
Roula Khalaf, Editor of the FT, selects her favourite stories in this weekly newsletter.
From the CFTC’s chair and sole commissioner Michael Selig:
Today, perpetual futures contracts on individual equity securities (the “Equity Perps”) can begin trading for the first time on CFTC-registered exchanges.
In my inaugural remarks, I directed the CFTC to use the tools at its disposal to onshore perpetual derivative products so that they can flourish in the U.S., subject to appropriate safeguards. Earlier this year, the CFTC took historic action in this regard by approving the listing of the first true bitcoin perpetual futures contract on a CFTC-regulated exchange.
Today’s announcement builds on that milestone by extending the availability of the perpetual futures contract instrument in the U.S. beyond digital commodities and into traditional securities. This expansion marks a significant step towards allowing U.S. market participants, consistent with applicable law, to avail themselves of the advantages of perpetual futures that have led to their emergence as widely sought tools for risk-management and price-discovery. I believe that bringing these types of innovative products into our regulated markets ensures that American investors and traders can access these products within the protections of the CFTC’s proven regulatory framework, rather than being forced to turn to offshore, and often unregulated, venues.
The Equity Perps were deemed approved by the Commission, pursuant to Commission Regulation 40.3, as security futures products under the Commodity Futures Modernization Act of 2000 (the “CFMA”). The contracts are thus subject to the applicable requirements of the Commodity Exchange Act, the U.S. Federal securities laws, and the regulatory frameworks of both the CFTC and the SEC.
More than two decades ago, Congress enacted the CFMA to establish a framework for the joint regulation of security futures products. This framework recognized the complementary roles of the CFTC and SEC in overseeing American financial markets by providing a pathway for innovation at the intersection of the U.S. Federal commodity laws and the U.S. Federal securities laws. Earlier this year, and in furtherance of those principles, the CFTC and SEC entered into a historic memorandum of understanding (the “MOU”) to guide coordination and collaboration between the two agencies.
The Equity Perps build on the foundation of the CFMA and the MOU. For too long, regulatory uncertainty left innovative products, such as security futures and equity perpetual futures, stranded in what SEC Chairman Paul S. Atkins has aptly described as a regulatory “no man’s land” due to a lack of harmonization between the agencies. The CFTC and SEC have turned the page on that era, and are committed to delivering regulatory clarity for innovative products and a clear path to market, rather than more casualties of jurisdictional disputes.
The Equity Perps demonstrate the strength of the ongoing commitments of the CFTC and SEC to support lawful innovation, uphold market integrity, and ensure investor and customer protection through the harmonization of the CFTC’s and SEC’s regulatory frameworks.
I would like to thank the many dedicated staff at the CFTC for their continued hard work and collaboration with the SEC. And I look forward to building on today’s milestone as the CFTC works to ensure that the new frontier of finance is built in the United States of America.

articles.full_text:
The Morning Bull - Australian Market Morning Update Thursday, 5 Nov 2026
Australian shares are set for a cautious, slightly softer open, with sentiment dominated by fresh signs of domestic slowdown. The key driver today is the slide in Australia’s October composite and services PMIs into contraction territory.
The S&P Global Flash Composite PMI printed at 48.5 in October, while the Services PMI matched that 48.5 reading after previously holding above 50. Both readings point to shrinking private activity and indicate weaker momentum heading into year end.
When activity surveys slip below 50, banks and investors tend to reassess borrowing and earnings assumptions. Softer demand can limit pricing power, squeeze margins in manufacturing and construction, and pressure cash flows that underpin hiring and new investment plans.
The open question now is whether this weakness is a brief soft patch or the start of a more persistent slowdown. Tomorrow’s Australia trade balance data will test that view by revealing how exports and domestic demand are holding up.
Advertisement
Stocks to Watch Before the Opening Bell
Scentre Group (SCG)
Scentre Group released an operating update that pointed to higher customer visits, strong specialty store sales and occupancy at 99.8%. Management also reaffirmed 2026 FFO and distribution guidance. At the same time, David Jones heading for administration puts A$45 million of rent at risk. Watch how leasing spreads, redevelopment progress and any re-leasing of those stores evolve.
Vicinity Centres (VCX)
The expected administration of David Jones puts Vicinity Centres in focus because department store closures could free large blocks of mall space. That can pressure rents in the short term. It can also create chances to remix centres with new tenants. Pay attention to any disclosure on vacancy, re-leasing timelines and how Vicinity positions its key flagship locations.
Reliance Worldwide (RWC)
Reliance Worldwide has mailed the Scheme Booklet for the proposed Brookfield Capital Partners takeover, and the Federal Court has signed off on a 4 December Scheme Meeting. This moves the deal into the decision phase. Readers should watch the Independent Expert’s conclusions, voting turnout and any change in terms or competing offers before that deadline.
Top Movers
NEXTDC (ASX:NXT) climbed 4.15% as traders reassessed executive pay concerns ahead of the upcoming remuneration vote.
BCI Minerals (ASX:BCI) advanced 3.88% after BMO Capital initiated coverage with an Outperform rating and A$0.60 price target.
EQ Resources (ASX:EQR) gained 3.70% following BMO Capital's new Outperform initiation and A$0.55 target on the company.
Top Losers
4DMedical (ASX:4DX) fell 10.79% after the company addressed an ASX price query and recent trading volatility.
Silex Systems (ASX:SLX) fell 9.58%.
Champion Iron (ASX:CIA) fell 4.85% after Scotiabank reduced its price target to C$3.50 from C$4.
On The Radar
Australian bank earnings and fresh trade data take centre stage over the next few sessions, with US labour and inflation prints adding a global layer for local rates and currency expectations.
Australia Balance of Trade, Thu 5 Nov. Forecast points to an A$1b trade surplus for September against a prior A$0.495b, so a stronger surplus would underline export support for miners and the Australian dollar, while a weaker result would highlight softer external demand.
National Australia Bank, Thu 5 Nov. Full year 2026 results land today, and the interest margin and loan impairment charges will show how higher borrowing costs and softer domestic activity are feeding into profitability and credit quality across the lending book.
REA Group, Thu 5 Nov. Q1 2027 numbers arrive pre market, with listing volumes and depth advertising revenue giving a direct read on Australian housing activity and the resilience of digital property advertising spend.
Macquarie Group, Fri 6 Nov. First half 2027 earnings will focus on performance fees and commodities trading income, which together shape the volatility of the group result and often steer sentiment toward diversified financials in Australia.
US Non Farm Payrolls and Unemployment Rate, Fri 6 Nov. Consensus looks for 65,000 new jobs and a 4.2% unemployment rate for October, so a stronger labour print would support a firmer US dollar and tighter global financial conditions for Australian borrowers.
Sector & Industry Watch
Real Estate Retail REITs juggle rates and tenants
Real Estate has gained ground over the past week, helped by a roughly 4% 7 day rise, yet 12 month returns are still weaker. Shopping centre landlords such as Scentre Group and Vicinity Centres are dealing with David Jones heading for administration at the same time the sector enjoys a 30 day rebound.
If you own retail REITs for income, the practical issue is how long big boxes sit empty and on what rent new tenants sign. Listen for commentary on reletting timelines, incentives and redevelopment plans in updates from Scentre, Vicinity and peers, since that goes straight to cash flow and future distributions.
Energy Pullback tests holders after strong year
Energy has slipped over the last 7 days, with the sector down close to 4% for the week after strong year to date and 12 month gains. Weaker global oil prices have weighed on producers while news flow stays busy, from Woodside Energy’s North West Shelf stake reshuffle to helium focused capital raisings at Gold Hydrogen and Blue Star Helium.
If your portfolio mixes fuel producers with airlines or transport, tonight’s official US crude inventory numbers are the swing factor. A sharp move in the oil price after those figures can quickly change earnings expectations for ASX energy stocks and margin assumptions for Qantas, Virgin and logistics exposed retailers.
Materials and Metals and Mining Miners soften despite busy project news
Materials and Metals and Mining have eased over the past week and month, even though 1 year returns remain positive for both indices. Heavyweights such as BHP have come under pressure while smaller stocks issue a steady stream of drilling results, capital raisings and critical minerals updates across gold, copper, rare earths and tungsten.
If you hold a cluster of miners, Thursday’s Australia Balance of Trade release is the key macro check. Export values for iron ore, coal and base metals will give a clearer read on offshore demand that underpins many of these project announcements and may help explain whether recent weakness is mostly sentiment driven.
Banks have pushed higher over the past 7 days and month while 1 year returns stay close to flat for the sector. A 4.85% cash rate is flowing straight into higher home loan repayments as the big four, including National Australia Bank, pass on the full hike, which supports interest income but tightens household budgets.
If you rely on bank dividends, National Australia Bank’s full year 2026 result on Thursday is the clearest signal to watch. Arrears, hardship requests and bad debt charges will show how stressed borrowers are and how much flexibility boards may feel they have around future payout settings.
Healthcare and Pharmaceuticals & Biotech Product milestones steady a choppy year
Healthcare and Pharmaceuticals & Biotech have been edging higher over the past month after a softer 12 month patch. Recent headlines range from Nanosonics’ FY26 revenue update and Micro X imaging progress to FDA related steps for Radiopharm Theranostics and Orthocell, as well as capital raisings and trial plans at smaller biotechs.
If you own Healthcare or Pharmaceuticals & Biotech stocks, focus on each company’s trial timelines, approvals and cash runway rather than macro prints. Upcoming clinical readouts, US clearances and funding moves usually drive share prices far more than PMI data and can quickly change the risk profile of a concentrated portfolio.
