articles.title: WTI edges up to near $96.00 as uncertainty persists over US-Iran peace prospects - www.tmgm.com
articles.summary: WTI edges up to near $96.00 as uncertainty persists over US-Iran peace prospects  www.tmgm.com
articles.full_text:
At around $96.10 per barrel in Wednesday’s Asian session, West Texas Intermediate (WTI) oil is advancing for a second consecutive day. The rise in crude prices comes as investors weigh uncertainty over the continuing peace talks between the US and Iran.
New proposals from mediators aimed at narrowing the two countries’ differences are being assessed by both sides, according to Qatar’s Foreign Ministry spokesperson. Iran’s national security chief, however, said in a social media post that Washington’s response was still unsatisfactory.
According to the Financial Times, Donald Trump said the US had no immediate plans to attack Iran and appeared to be securing what it wanted. Although the US was prepared to act if necessary, he added, there might be no need to do so. His remarks came despite Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu suggesting an attack could take place later this week.
Earlier this week, defensive US strikes on Iran targeted surface-to-air missile systems that had been used against American assets. Their restricted scope nevertheless points to no immediate resumption of large-scale military operations.
Despite the recovery, WTI, the US oil benchmark, is still around 6% lower so far this week. Hopes of a diplomatic breakthrough, coupled with indications that Middle Eastern crude exports are recovering, continue to underpin the weekly decline.
Among the crude oils traded internationally, WTI, short for West Texas Intermediate, is one of three principal types alongside Brent and Dubai Crude. Its relatively low gravity and sulphur content earn it the descriptions “light” and “sweet”, respectively. This high-quality oil is regarded as easy to refine. Produced in the United States, it is distributed through the Cushing hub, known as “The Pipeline Crossroads of the World”. WTI serves as an oil market benchmark, with its price regularly cited by the media.
Supply and demand determine WTI oil prices, as they do those of other assets. Stronger global growth can therefore lift demand, while weaker growth can have the reverse effect. Supply disruptions caused by political instability, wars or sanctions can also affect prices. Another important influence is the production policy of OPEC, a group of major oil-producing countries. As crude is traded predominantly in US Dollars, the currency’s value also matters for WTI: a weaker US Dollar can make oil more affordable, while a stronger one can make it less so.
WTI oil prices respond to the weekly inventory figures released by the American Petroleum Institute (API) and the Energy Information Agency (EIA). Stock movements signal changes in the balance of supply and demand. A drawdown can point to stronger demand and lift oil prices, whereas a build in stocks can indicate greater supply and weigh on prices. The API publishes its report every Tuesday, followed by the EIA the next day. The two sets of figures tend to be similar: they are within 1% of each other 75% of the time. As the EIA is a government agency, its data is regarded as more reliable.
At meetings held twice a year, the 12 oil-producing nations that make up OPEC (Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries) jointly set production quotas for members. These decisions frequently influence WTI oil prices. A reduction in quotas can restrict supply and lift prices; an increase in OPEC production has the reverse effect. The wider OPEC+ grouping brings in ten additional countries outside OPEC, with Russia the most prominent.

articles.title: 10-Year Treasury Yield Long-Term Perspective: October 2026 - Advisor Perspectives
articles.summary: 10-Year Treasury Yield Long-Term Perspective: October 2026  Advisor Perspectives
articles.full_text:
This article looks at the 10-year Treasury yield's historical trends since 1962, exploring its relationship with key economic indicators like the Fed Funds Rate (FFR), inflation, and the S&P 500.
Fighting Inflation vs. Stimulating Recovery
The 10-year Treasury yield has experienced dramatic fluctuations, ranging from a peak of 15.68% in October 1981, during the height of the Volcker era, to a historic low of 0.55% in August 2020, amidst the economic uncertainty of the pandemic. More recently, at the end of October 2026, the weekly average stood at 4.99%.
The stagflation crisis of the late 1970s and early 1980s demanded drastic measures. To combat soaring prices, Federal Reserve Chairman Paul Volcker pushed the Federal Funds Rate (FFR) to a historic high of 20.06% in January 1981. This aggressive tightening of monetary policy was instrumental in curbing runaway inflation, albeit at the cost of a significant economic slowdown. Nine months later, in October 1981, the 10-year yield's weekly average hit a peak of 15.68%.
In stark contrast, the FFR was driven to near-zero levels in the aftermath of the 2008 financial crisis and again during the economic turmoil of the 2020 pandemic. Specifically, the FFR reached a record low of approximately 0.04% in May 2020. A few months later, the 10-year yield weekly average fell to a historic low of 0.55% in August. These periods of ultra-low interest rates aimed to stimulate borrowing, investment, and economic recovery.
The Recent Surge and Policy Response
This period of ultra-low rates was followed by inflation reaching its highest levels since the aforementioned stagflation crisis. In response, the Fed began raising rates to fight inflation, though some would argue their efforts were too late. From May 2022 to August 2023, the Fed quickly raised the FFR to its highest level in over 20 years. The 10-year yield moved in similar fashion, tracking the sharp rise in the FFR.
The Fed then held its rate steady for just over a year as inflation cooled from its 2022 peak. However, the central bank shifted course in September 2024, implementing three consecutive rate cuts. Interestingly, while the FFR declined during the back end of 2024, the 10-year yield moved in the opposite direction and inflation remained sticky.
In 2025, the Fed maintained steady rates for the first half of the year before implementing three consecutive rate cuts to close out the year. Meanwhile, the 10-year yield has steadily risen, as the FFR has been raised. Despite these rate moves, inflation heated up for most of the year, remaining well above the Fed's 2% target. At the end of October, the 10-year yield weekly average stood at 4.99% while inflation was at 3.74%.
At their most recent meeting, the Federal Reserve elected to hold the federal funds rate at 3.75%–4%. The decision, which markets had largely priced in, comes after the first benchmark rate since 2023.
In a statement, the Committee noted, "Economic activity is expanding at a strong pace," but "inflation remains elevated." They stated that they will "deliver price stability."
The Fed will meet again in December where they are expected to raise by another 25 basis points. At the time of writing, the CMEFedWatch Tool shows a 79% likelihood the Fed will raise rates versus a 21% likelihood of keeping rates where they are.
Treasuries vs. Equities
In our next chart, the S&P 500 is overlaid with the 10-year yield’s weekly average and the Fed Funds Rate. Generally, equities and treasuries tend to move in opposite directions. When one goes up; the other goes down. However, that’s not always the case. During inflationary periods, like the past few years, both move in tandem due to the impact of higher interest rates on corporate profits and bond prices. The initial chart presents nominal values, meaning it doesn't account for inflation. This can create a misleading picture of the actual purchasing power of yields and equity returns.

ASX slides as Democrats’ success flusters Wall Street; oil stocks gain
Updated ,first published
The Australian sharemarket extended its losses on Wednesday afternoon as investors digested the latest rate hike by the Reserve Bank and US market futures fell in response to the Democratic landslide in the US midterm elections.
The S&P/ASX 200 finished down 52.30 points, or 0.6 per cent, at 8834.50. Seven of its 11 sectors were in the red, while energy stocks benefited from a higher oil price, tech stocks tracked overnight gains by Big Tech on Wall Street, and defensive trades lifted utilities and consumer staples.
The Australian dollar rose to US69.76¢. The ASX added 0.3 per cent on Tuesday, with the RBA signalling a wait-and-see approach for the months ahead after raising rates to an 18-year high.
A projected Democratic sweep of both houses of Congress rippled across global markets, sending stocks and the US dollar lower while boosting US Treasuries, on speculation the result would put the brakes on President Donald Trump’s agenda. Wall Street generally prefers split control of Washington, which it sees as offering less risk of transformative policies that hurt business.
Futures for the S&P 500 Index dropped 1.2 per cent and those for the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 fell 2 per cent, suggesting sharp losses when Wall Street opens. Investors see a Democratic win as a potential setback for stocks given the prospect of tighter regulatory scrutiny, particularly of high-growth technology and artificial intelligence companies that have been driving global markets this year. Treasuries, meanwhile, stand to benefit if political gridlock limits further tax cuts and government spending, easing concerns about federal borrowing.
“A stronger Democratic showing is adding to market uncertainty, particularly over the prospect of tighter corporate regulation and greater scrutiny of AI spending,” said Dilin Wu, a strategist at Pepperstone Group in Melbourne. “But with tech valuations already under pressure, the election is amplifying existing concerns rather than driving the sell-off on its own.”
On the ASX, the tech sector pared back its morning gains, with WiseTech finishing down 0.3 per cent and fellow software maker Technology One down 1.1 per cent – affected also by news that Australian software success story Canva is slashing 22 per cent of its jobs as AI alternatives dent its growth. Cloud connections provider Megaport lost 2.7 per cent, while data centre firm NextDC still jumped 4.2 per cent, keeping the sector in the green.
Consumer discretionary stocks finished lower, paring back their rally from Tuesday afternoon, when investors waded into the sector on hopes the RBA has ended its cycle of rate rises after its five demand-sapping hikes this year. JB Hi-Fi lost 2 per cent, Eagers Automotive shed 3.6 per cent and Harvey Norman was down 1.1 per cent.
The mining sector also declined. Copper heavyweights BHP and Rio Tinto dropped 1.5 per cent and 1.7 per cent, respectively as the red metal slumped to a seven-week low as traders reassessed the AI trade. Iron ore miner Fortescue fell 1.5 per cent. Gold miner Northern Star Resources lost 2 per cent.
The Big Four banks were mixed, with CBA falling 0.6 per cent, but National Australia Bank and Westpac both finishing 0.5 per cent higher and ANZ Bank up 0.1 per cent.
Energy stocks rose after oil prices edged higher overnight following a two-day decline, as traders weighed the outlook for the US-Iran war following conflicting signals on the trajectory of peace talks. Brent climbed above $US107 a barrel overnight before closing below $US104.
Tehran and Washington are reviewing fresh proposals on how to resolve their differences, according to a diplomat briefed on the matter. Still, Iran’s national security chief said on X that the US response has so far been “not satisfactory”.
Woodside and Santos both gained 1 per cent, while Ampol was up 1.4 per cent. As the oil stocks rebounded, companies with big fuel bills declined. Qantas Airways slumped 4.9 per cent and Virgin Australia fell 4.1 per cent in reversal of their rally on Tuesday when oil prices eased.
Defensive sectors also benefited, with the nation’s biggest supermarket chain Woolworths up 1.3 per cent and power giant Origin gaining 1.9 per cent.
On Wall Street overnight, the S&P 500 rose 0.4 per cent. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was down 0.4 per cent, and the Nasdaq composite finished 0.8 per cent higher. Indexes were lower across Europe and mixed in Asia.
With AP, Bloomberg.
The Market Recap newsletter is a wrap of the day’s trading. Get it each weekday afternoon.

articles.title: Here’s What Fewer Fed Rate Votes Could Mean for Borrowers - themortgagepoint.com
articles.summary: Here’s What Fewer Fed Rate Votes Could Mean for Borrowers  themortgagepoint.com
articles.full_text:
Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh announced after last week’s FOMC meeting that the central bank plans to reduce the number of rate-setting votes over the next two years.
CNBC reported that some experts believe the move could potentially extend the timeline for everyday Americans to see borrowing costs adjust.
“Fewer Fed meetings in 2027 could mean consumers wait longer to see relief when borrowing costs are elevated,” said James Vrachas, Executive Director at advisory firm Post Oak Group.
CNBC noted that while Americans may feel removed from the Fed, the central bank’s moves ripple through many consumer products, including borrowing rates for credit cards, home loans, and auto financing.
For example, CNBC said that most credit cards have variable rates tied to the prime rate, which moves with the Fed’s benchmark. However, even with the central bank holding rates unchanged, credit card rates are edging higher as issuers protect themselves from risk, according to LendingTree.
Reduced Exposure
Card issuers are reducing their exposure to borrowers who may fall behind on payments or default amid stubborn inflation in everyday expenses, said Matt Schulz, LendingTree’s Chief Credit Analyst.
In addition, card issuers are generally slow to cut rates unless the Fed prompts them.
“Issuers will tinker with rates a bit at the margins at other times, but the big moves tend to only come when issuers are pushed,” Schulz noted.
On Oct. 28, the Fed voted to keep its benchmark borrowing rate at the current target range of 3.75% to 4% as policymakers deliberated next steps with inflation remaining well above the Fed’s 2% goal.
Warsh said the Fed will keep meeting eight times a year, but he said at the news conference following the October meeting, but he said that next year, one of the eight meetings will not entail a vote on interest rates or include a post-meeting statement.
Only 6 Rate Vote Opportunities
He said the “strategy” meetings will increase to two the following year. That leaves just six opportunities to adjust rates—except in emergency meetings, if necessary.
“For consumers, that could mean longer periods of uncertainty around borrowing costs,” said Jordan Ricciardi, a Senior Wealth Strategy Associate at UBS. “Our clients looking to buy a home, refinance a mortgage or finance a business could be impacted as fewer scheduled opportunities means the Fed isn’t as quickly responding to changing economic conditions.”
Fewer scheduled opportunities to adjust rates means borrowing rates could remain stubbornly high even if economic conditions begin to improve, Post Oak Group’s Vrachas said.
Vrachas noted that as it stands, financial institutions can adjust rates whenever market conditions warrant, regardless of the Fed’s meeting schedule. In the interim, many consumers may continue to face elevated borrowing costs for mortgages, car loans and credit card debt, among other financial products.
“For consumers, the bigger concern isn’t necessarily fewer meetings, but whether lenders pass along lower borrowing costs as quickly as they pass along increases,” Vrachas said.
CNBC noted that consumers could even be more affected by the lack of transparency, as Warsh implements measures to curtail so-called forward guidance, or how the Fed signals its future rate moves.
Cards Close to His Vest
Even as economic conditions have become more complicated and information is more widely available, “Warsh keeps his proverbial cards closer to his chest than his recent predecessors have,” said Mark Hamrick, an Economic Analyst and Founder of The Hamrick Brief, a weekly newsletter.
“I wouldn’t expect consumers to see the universe of market rates change simply because the Fed votes less often,” he said. “But the public may have less opportunity to hear from the source about how and why the Fed is making the decisions that shape what they pay to borrow and what they earn on their savings.”
In the interim, “the best protection for consumers remains shopping around, particularly for the highest yields among savings accounts and [certificates of deposit],” Hamrick noted.
As long as the Fed keeps rates unchanged, some top-yielding online savings accounts are offering interest rates as high as 4% or more, Bankrate data shows.
“That’s one of the upsides of an elevated interest rate environment: savers can earn meaningfully higher yields,” Hamrick said.

articles.full_text:
With inflation largely driven by supply pressures and expectations remaining anchored, according to BNY Markets’ John Velis, he questions whether higher interest rates can tackle those pressures. Nevertheless, following the Federal Reserve’s latest decision to hold rates, he continues to expect one further increase in December to safeguard its credibility. The outlook becomes less clear heading into 2027, with Velis warning that demand-side risks could warrant further tightening later.
"After last week’s anticipated hold by the FOMC, we maintain our view that there will be one additional rate hike in December this year, to preserve Fed credibility. Heading into 2027, the landscape appears much murkier."
"Yes, inflation remains high, and the recent bout of higher oil prices will undoubtedly keep the pressure on prices. We’ve argued, and continue to argue, that inflation is mainly supply driven, and that inflation expectations remain well anchored over long horizons."
"We’re not convinced that higher rates will be able to rein in supply pressures, as they are indeed a demand-management tool. Nevertheless, it bears watching to see if demand-side pressures emerge in 2027, in which case interest rate remedies would be appropriate."
"We noted with some interest Warsh’s assertion at last week’s press conference that the interest rate hike in September tightened financial conditions meaningfully, since aside from the AI-related wobbles in October, there’s scant evidence of such tightening pervading across the real economy."
"Still, should financial jitters persist, conditions will naturally tighten, requiring fewer hikes in 2027 than the two currently priced in."

articles.title: Mortgage Rates Are Falling Even as a December Fed Hike Looms - Norada Real Estate Investments
articles.summary: Mortgage Rates Are Falling Even as a December Fed Hike Looms  Norada Real Estate Investments
articles.full_text:
rates are falling even as a December Fed hike looms, and that sounds like it shouldn't be possible. Freddie Mac's weekly survey shows the average 30-year fixed rate slipped to 7.24% on October 29, down from 7.32% a week earlier and 7.40% in mid-October. Freddie Mac called it the lowest level of the month. At the same time, the Federal Reserve kept its benchmark rate at 3.75%–4.00% on October 28, but two officials voted to raise it, and markets now see about a 76% chance of a quarter-point hike on December 9.
So which signal should you trust? The short answer is that rates take their cue from the bond market, not directly from the Fed. Over the past few weeks, the 10-year Treasury yield has dropped from 5.31% in early October to 4.91% on November 2. That slide is what's pulling home loan rates down, even with the Fed leaning toward one more increase.
In this article, I'll walk you through why these two trends can move in opposite directions, what a December hike could really mean for your monthly payment, and how to think about locking a rate right now.
Mortgage Rates Are Falling Even as a December Fed Hike Looms
Let's start with the numbers, because they tell a clear story. Every major mortgage measure I track pulled back in late October.
- Freddie Mac: The 30-year fixed averaged 7.24% on October 29, after back-to-back 7.40% readings on October 8 and 15. The 15-year fixed fell to 6.60% from 6.68%.
- Mortgage Bankers Association: The 30-year conforming rate in MBA's weekly survey dropped to 7.37% from 7.41%, the lowest in three weeks.
- 10-year Treasury: The yield settled at 4.91% on November 2, down from 5.31% on October 5.
That's real relief, but let's keep it in perspective. A year ago, Freddie Mac's 30-year average was 6.17%. Rates are easing from a high level, not returning to cheap money.
Why Mortgage Rates Follow the 10-Year Treasury
Here's the part that confuses a lot of people. The Fed sets the federal funds rate, which is what banks charge each other for overnight loans. That rate shapes short-term borrowing like credit cards, auto loans and home equity lines of credit. A 30-year mortgage is a very different animal.
Most mortgages get bundled and sold to investors as bonds. Those investors compare them with other long-term safe bets, and the 10-year Treasury is the main yardstick. Since many homeowners sell or refinance within about ten years, a 30-year mortgage behaves a lot like a 10-year bond. When the 10-year yield goes up, lenders raise mortgage rates. When it falls, mortgage rates usually follow.
Think of the Fed as the driver of a city bus and the bond market as the weather. The driver controls the speed on city streets. But on the highway, wind and rain decide how fast everyone travels. Mortgage rates live on the highway.
The Gap Between the 10-Year and Mortgage Rates
On October 29, Freddie Mac's 30-year rate sat about 2.26 percentage points above the 10-year Treasury yield of 4.98% that day. That gap, often called the spread, covers lender costs, investor risk and the chance that borrowers pay off early. When markets calm down, the spread can narrow, which gives mortgage rates a little extra room to fall.
The weekly numbers line up closely:
| Week (Thursday) | Freddie Mac 30-Year | 10-Year Treasury Yield | 
|---|---|---|
| September 24 | 7.03% | 5.18% | 
| October 1 | 7.28% | 5.24% | 
| October 8 | 7.40% | 5.22% | 
| October 15 | 7.40% | 5.10% | 
| October 22 | 7.32% | 4.96% | 
| October 29 | 7.24% | 4.98% | 
Source: Freddie Mac, U.S. Treasury
What the Bond Market Is Telling Us
Bond yields fall when investors want safety or expect slower growth. Recent data has given them reasons to lean that way. In its October statement, the Fed said “inflation remains elevated,” and Chair Kevin Warsh pointed out that higher bond yields had already tightened financial conditions. In plain English, the market did some of the Fed's work for it.
Notice something interesting about the yield curve, too. On November 2, the 2-year Treasury yield rose to 4.59% while the 10-year fell to 4.91%. Short-term yields are reacting to hike talk. Long-term yields are more focused on where the economy is headed over many years. That split is exactly why your mortgage rate can drop while the Fed debates raising rates.
How Likely Is a December Hike?
The Fed's next meeting is December 8–9, and it will include fresh economic projections. As of November 3, market pricing tracked by RateProbability shows about a 76% chance of a quarter-point hike, which would lift the target range to 4.00%–4.25%. That's lower than the roughly 85% odds right after the October meeting, but it's still a strong lean.
The October vote matters here. According to the Fed's statement, the decision to hold passed 10–2, with Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack preferring a hike. Two dissents in favor of tighter policy is a signal markets don't ignore.
What a December Hike Could Do to Your Mortgage
This is where many people expect the worst. But if the hike happens as expected, much of it is already baked into today's rates. Markets price in likely moves ahead of time, so a well-telegraphed quarter-point increase often causes little change in rates on the day it happens.
What could move mortgage rates more is the message. If the Fed signals several more hikes in 2027, bond yields could climb and mortgage rates could rise with them. If it hints that one more hike is enough, yields could keep easing. In other words, watch the tone and the projections, not just the decision.
The bigger impact of a hike lands on short-term debt. Credit card rates and home equity lines usually adjust within a billing cycle or two. Adjustable-rate can also feel it at their next reset.
What the Drop Means in Dollars
On a $400,000 , principal and interest at 7.40% come to about $2,770 a month. At 7.24%, the payment falls to about $2,726. That's roughly $44 less every month, or more than $500 a year, just from the move over the last few weeks.
Compare that with a year ago, though. At 6.17%, the same loan cost about $2,442 a month. Today's buyer still pays around $284 more each month than someone who bought last fall.
Taxes, insurance and mortgage insurance can change the picture a lot. If you'd like your full monthly cost with those added in, scroll down to the calculator just above our related reading list and enter your own numbers.
More Buyers Are Turning to ARMs
Borrowers are already hunting for ways to trim payments. MBA reports that the adjustable-rate share of applications rose to 11.3%, its highest level in more than a year. The average 5/1 ARM rate in that survey was 6.41%, nearly a full percentage point below the 30-year fixed.
An ARM can make sense if you plan to move or refinance within a few years. Just remember that the rate can reset higher later, and a Fed that's still hiking adds to that risk.
Lock Now or Float? How to Think It Through
Nobody can promise where rates go next, so I won't pretend to. But here's a balanced way to weigh the choice.
Locking may make more sense if:
- You're closing within the next 30 to 45 days.
- Today's payment already fits your budget comfortably.
- A jump of a quarter point would strain your finances.
Floating may make more sense if:
- Your closing date is weeks away and you can handle some risk.
- Your lender offers a float-down option at a fair price.
- You're comfortable if rates rise instead of falling.
Either way, compare quotes from several lenders on the same day and check the fees, not just the rate. This is general information, so talk with a loan officer about your own situation.
This Week's Data to Watch
A busy calendar could nudge both bond yields and December hike odds. All times are Eastern.
- Tuesday, November 3: JOLTS job openings report, 10:00 a.m.
- Wednesday, November 4: ADP private payrolls at 8:15 a.m., MBA mortgage applications, and the ISM services survey at 10:00 a.m.
- Thursday, November 5: Freddie Mac's weekly mortgage rate survey and weekly jobless claims.
- Friday, November 6: The October jobs report at 8:30 a.m., the last big labor reading before the December meeting.
A hot jobs report could push yields and hike odds higher. A soft one could extend the recent mortgage rate slide.
My Take
The headline sounds like a contradiction, but it isn't. The Fed may raise its short-term rate in December, while bond investors are already pulling long-term rates lower. For home buyers, that's a small window of relief worth paying attention to. Don't count on a big drop, keep a close eye on Friday's jobs report, and make your decision based on a payment you can live with.

articles.title: Standard Lithium Ltd. Faces Continued Pressure as Lithium Market Dynamics and Development Execution Risks Weigh on Equity - kalkine.ca
articles.summary: Standard Lithium Ltd. Faces Continued Pressure as Lithium Market Dynamics and Development Execution Risks Weigh on Equity  kalkine.ca
articles.full_text:
Key Highlights
- Stock Performance: Standard Lithium Ltd. closed down -4.43% on November 2, 2026, as the lithium sector continued to face investor caution amid Commodity price uncertainty.
- Sentiment & Momentum: The lithium market has experienced meaningful price Volatility in recent periods, creating a challenging backdrop for development-stage lithium projects and their Equity valuations.
- Sector Dynamics: Lithium project developers are at a pivotal juncture where feasibility milestones and project financing are critical valuation catalysts, but the path to production involves extended timelines and Capital intensity.
- Project Stage: Standard Lithium's Arkansas lithium project, which completed a feasibility study, represents an advanced-stage development asset, but advancing from feasibility to construction and production requires significant additional capital commitments.
Introduction
Standard Lithium Ltd. (TSX:SLI) is an advanced-stage lithium development company focused on the commercialization of its Arkansas Lithium Project, located in southern Arkansas, United States. The project utilizes direct lithium extraction (DLE) technology applied to lithium-bearing brine resources in the region. Standard Lithium filed a feasibility study for the Arkansas project, marking a significant milestone in advancing the asset toward potential production. The company targets production of battery-grade lithium compounds for use in electric vehicle battery Supply chains and other lithium-ion applications.
Shares of Standard Lithium Ltd. declined -4.43% on November 2, 2026, reflecting the challenging conditions that have characterized the lithium Investment landscape. The company occupies an advanced position in its project development cycle relative to earlier-stage lithium explorers, having completed a feasibility study, but the gap between feasibility completion and construction commencement represents a critical and capital-intensive phase that generates ongoing investor uncertainty.
Key Reasons Behind Decline
The pullback in Standard Lithium shares on November 2, 2026, stems from several factors that continue to shape the lithium sector investment environment and the company's specific development situation.
- Lithium Price Market Conditions: Lithium prices have experienced significant volatility in the period following the initial electric vehicle-driven Demand surge, with supply capacity additions in multiple regions contributing to pricing pressure. When lithium spot and contract prices weaken, the economic projections underpinning project development decisions are re-evaluated by investors, creating downward pressure on development-stage lithium company valuations.
- Project Financing and Capital Requirements: Advancing the Arkansas Lithium Project from a completed feasibility study into construction requires arranging substantial project financing, which may include a combination of debt, equity, and strategic partner capital. The process of securing project-scale financing is complex, time-consuming, and uncertain in outcome. Market Participants closely watch for progress on financing arrangements, and any perceived delays or complications create valuation headwinds.
- DLE Technology Commercialization Risk: Direct lithium extraction is a relatively newer approach to lithium production compared to conventional evaporation pond methods used extensively in South America. While DLE offers potential advantages in Recovery Rate and environmental footprint, investors assess the commercial-scale performance and cost efficiency of DLE operations with caution until a larger number of projects demonstrate proven production at scale, contributing to a technology risk discount on DLE-focused developers.
- Broader Mining and Battery Materials Sector Weakness: Mining sector equities and battery materials developers faced sector-wide selling on November 2, 2026, as macro uncertainty and commodity demand concerns weighed on investor sentiment across resource equities. Development-stage companies without near-term production cash flows are typically more susceptible to these sentiment-driven corrections than producing resource companies.
- Electric Vehicle Demand Growth Rate Uncertainty: Lithium demand is substantially driven by battery production for electric vehicles. Any signal that EV adoption is growing more slowly than previously projected — whether from macroeconomic factors, policy changes, or competitive dynamics in the EV market — affects the long-term demand assumptions that support lithium project valuations and investment decisions.
Risks to Consider
Investors evaluating Standard Lithium should consider a range of material risks associated with the company's development-stage position and the volatile lithium market environment.
- Lithium Price Risk: The Economics of the Arkansas Lithium Project are sensitive to prevailing and projected lithium prices. Sustained weakness in lithium pricing could alter the financial returns projected in the feasibility study and affect the attractiveness of the project to potential financing partners and strategic investors.
- Project Financing Risk: Securing the capital required to advance the Arkansas project from feasibility through construction involves complex negotiations with potential Debt providers, equity partners, and strategic industry participants. There is no certainty that financing will be arranged on terms that are favorable to existing shareholders or within anticipated timelines.
- Construction and Execution Risk: Transitioning from a completed feasibility study to construction and production commissioning involves significant execution risk, including potential cost overruns, engineering challenges, supply chain variability, and the inherent complexities of deploying DLE technology at commercial scale for the first time.
- Regulatory and Permitting Risk: The Arkansas project requires relevant state and federal permits and regulatory approvals for construction and operation. Environmental review processes, water management regulations, and land use considerations in Arkansas could affect the timeline or scope of project development.
- Strategic Partner Dependency: Standard Lithium has historically operated in the context of strategic partnerships and potential joint development arrangements. The company's project advancement may depend on the participation and capital commitment of strategic partners, and changes in partner strategies or financial circumstances could affect the pace and structure of project development.
Valuation Perspective
Standard Lithium's valuation reflects both the completion of a meaningful project milestone — the Arkansas feasibility study — and the significant residual risk of advancing from feasibility to operational production. Development-stage lithium companies with completed feasibility studies are valued against project net present value calculations that are highly sensitive to assumed lithium prices, capital costs, and operating cost assumptions.
The current lithium Market Price environment has compressed net present value estimates across the lithium development sector, applying pressure to valuations even for projects that have achieved meaningful technical milestones. For Standard Lithium, the path to a valuation re-rating will require visible progress on financing arrangements, construction commencement, and ultimately production of battery-grade lithium from the Arkansas project.
Outlook
The long-term strategic case for Standard Lithium rests on growing demand for domestically produced battery materials in North America, supported by policy initiatives aimed at building resilient electric vehicle supply chains. The Arkansas Lithium Project's US location positions it to potentially benefit from battery material sourcing incentives and domestic lithium production support.
Near-term performance will be shaped by project financing progress, construction timeline visibility, lithium market price developments, and the broader EV adoption trajectory as a demand driver. Any announcements related to strategic Partnership developments or construction readiness would represent significant catalysts for the stock.

articles.title: Hong Kong Stock Price Limits: Complete Guide to Risks and Opportunities Without Daily Trading Halts - Longbridge
articles.summary: Hong Kong Stock Price Limits: Complete Guide to Risks and Opportunities Without Daily Trading Halts  Longbridge
articles.full_text:
Hong Kong Stocks Without Price Limits: The Complete Guide to Managing Risks and Seizing Opportunities
Unlike A-shares with daily limits, HK stocks have no price restrictions. Explore the Exchange's Volatility Control Mechanism (VCM), circuit breaker rules, penny stock and short-selling risks, and practical risk management for this unrestricted market.
TL;DR: Hong Kong stocks have no daily price limit restrictions, and stock prices can theoretically rise or fall significantly in a single trading day. Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing Limited has established a "Market Volatility Adjustment Mechanism" (VCM, colloquially known as the cooling-off period) to provide a buffer, but this is not equivalent to daily price limits. Investors must understand the risks involved and establish appropriate order placement habits.
Unlike Taiwan stocks and A-shares, which have daily price limit restrictions, Hong Kong stocks actually have no such concept of price limit restrictions: Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing Limited has not set daily percentage rise/fall limits on individual stocks or indices. This difference brings both higher price flexibility and greater volatility risk. The following breaks down the operational logic of Hong Kong stocks' lack of daily price limits, as well as the risks and market characteristics investors should be aware of.
Why Hong Kong Stocks Have No Daily Price Limit Restrictions
Hong Kong stocks adopt a free market pricing mechanism, where stock prices are determined by the supply and demand of buyers and sellers, with no daily percentage rise/fall ceiling. This contrasts with A-share main board (10% daily limit) and Taiwan stocks (10% daily price limit restrictions).
Coordination with T+0 Trading System
Hong Kong stocks operate under a T+0 trading system, allowing investors to sell on the same day after purchasing, providing greater flexibility in capital utilization but simultaneously requiring stronger real-time judgment abilities. To understand Hong Kong stock investment lot sizes, trading hours, and settlement arrangements, you can refer to the Hong Kong Stock Investment Beginner's Guide.
Main Risks Without Daily Price Limits
Without the protection of daily price limits, Hong Kong stocks and indices can experience significant volatility, and investors must face these relevant risks.
Stock Prices May Fluctuate Dramatically
Historically, Hong Kong stocks have recorded significant single-day swings when market sentiment reversed substantially, and individual stocks may also fluctuate significantly in a short period due to earnings announcements or regulatory news. Past market performance cannot serve as a guide to future results.
Additional Risks from Penny Stocks and Short Selling Mechanisms
Hong Kong's market permits short selling transactions. Individual companies with poor governance and frequent rights offerings (colloquially referred to as "penny stocks" in the market) may experience significant stock price declines in a short period once questioned. Some investors conduct thorough research on shareholding structures and financial conditions rather than making judgments based solely on price trends.
Volatility During Initial IPO Period
Hong Kong stocks have no daily price limit restrictions or temporary trading halts specifically for newly listed shares. The market volatility adjustment mechanism applies based on index constituent stocks and other lists. Newly listed shares generally must wait until they are included in the Hang Seng Composite Index constituent stock list before being added to the VCM securities list (Data source: Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing Limited VCM Mechanism Documentation). Stock prices may experience larger fluctuations during the initial listing period. Before participating in IPO subscriptions, you can refer to the New Share Subscription Basics Guide.
How the Market Volatility Adjustment Mechanism (VCM) Works
Although Hong Kong stocks have no daily price limits, Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing Limited established a "Market Volatility Adjustment Mechanism" (VCM) beginning in August 2016. According to the Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing Limited Trading Mechanism page, if the potential execution price of an applicable security deviates from the last traded price five minutes prior by more than a predetermined percentage, a 5-minute cooling-off period is triggered.
Triggering Thresholds Vary by Security Category
The VCM applies to Hang Seng Composite Large-cap, Mid-cap, and Small-cap Index constituent stocks, SPAC shares and warrants, as well as qualified exchange-traded funds and leveraged and inverse products. The triggering thresholds range from ±5% to ±50%; specifically, the thresholds for Hang Seng Composite Large-cap, Mid-cap, and Small-cap Index constituent stocks are ±10%, ±15%, and ±20% respectively (Data source: Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing Limited Trading Mechanism page, Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing Limited VCM Mechanism Documentation). During the cooling-off period, the system only accepts buy and sell orders within a specified price range and does not halt trading entirely.
Differences Between Cooling-off Period and Trading Halt
Trading continues during the VCM cooling-off period; however, newly entered buy and sell orders are restricted to a specified price range, whereas a trading halt suspends all trading entirely. The VCM applies only to designated periods within continuous trading sessions. After the cooling-off period, normal trading and VCM monitoring resume, and the same security can trigger the mechanism again within the same trading session. Investors can track real-time market movements through Longbridge Market Data Services.
Reminder: After the cooling-off period ends, price restrictions are lifted and stock prices can continue to fluctuate according to market supply and demand.
Market Characteristics Without Daily Price Limits
The absence of daily price limits also introduces certain structural characteristics to the market that investors should consider.
Prices May Reflect Information More Quickly
Unrestricted by daily percentage limits, the market can digest earnings announcements, regulatory news, and other information more rapidly, avoiding situations in some markets with daily price limits where stocks cannot be traded due to consecutive daily limit-down halts. However, when individual stocks lack sufficient liquidity, investors may still face difficulties executing trades at desired prices.
Diverse Range of Investment Instruments
The Hong Kong stock market encompasses stocks, ETFs, REITs, warrants, and callable bull/bear contracts and other diverse products. Warrants and callable bull/bear contracts are leveraged structural products with different pricing logic from traditional options. You can refer to Callable Bull/Bear Contracts Mechanism Explained in Detail and Warrant Investment Guide. Product details can be found on Longbridge Securities Product Overview page.
How Investors Can Manage Hong Kong Stock Volatility Risk
Facing a market without daily price limit protection, establishing appropriate order placement habits and risk management discipline is more important than chasing price fluctuations.
Differences Between Limit Orders and Market Orders
Using market orders may result in execution at unintended unfavorable prices during volatile periods. Limit orders allow investors to preset acceptable buy and sell prices in advance, reducing slippage risk, but may also fail to execute if prices don't reach the specified level. For details, see the Limit Orders vs. Market Orders Selection Guide.
Balancing Portfolio Diversification with Thorough Research
Individual stocks may fluctuate significantly due to sudden news. Some investors avoid concentrating funds in a single stock and conduct careful research before investing rather than relying solely on market news. Longbridge Securities' PortAI Investment Research Assistant can help users organize market information. For details, see Application of AI Investment Personalized Strategy.
Summary
Hong Kong stocks' "absence of daily price limits" is a double-edged sword: on one hand, it allows markets to reflect information more quickly, and combined with T+0 trading provides greater flexibility; on the other hand, it also means individual stocks and indices may experience more dramatic short-term fluctuations. Investors must face additional risks from penny stocks, short selling, and leveraged products. Understanding the VCM operational logic and risk management methods such as limit orders and portfolio diversification can help investors gain a more comprehensive understanding of Hong Kong stock trading risks.
Which tool to choose depends on your investment objectives, risk tolerance, market outlook, and experience level. Regardless of which investment tool you choose, you must fully understand its operational mechanism, risk characteristics, and trading rules, and establish a comprehensive risk management plan. articles.title: US midterms could trigger Treasury rally before debt crisis sends borrowing costs soaring - London Business News
articles.summary: US midterms could trigger Treasury rally before debt crisis sends borrowing costs soaring  London Business News
articles.full_text:
A Democratic victory in the US midterm elections could deliver a short-lived boost to government bonds before triggering a potentially damaging rise in borrowing costs, as Washington heads towards another confrontation over America’s mounting national debt, according to Nigel Green, chief executive of financial advisory group deVere.
Green believes investors may initially welcome the prospect of a divided Congress, anticipating that political gridlock will constrain major spending legislation and push Treasury yields lower.
But he warns that the apparent relief could prove temporary, with a looming debt-ceiling battle in 2027 potentially forcing Republicans and Democrats into an expensive compromise that leaves the federal government borrowing substantially more.
“The first instinct of bond investors will be to cheer gridlock,” Green said.
“A split Congress normally means fewer big spending bills, so yields will probably dip once the results are in.
“I think investors would be wrong to relax. This time, gridlock is likely to push US borrowing up, and markets aren’t pricing that yet.”
The warning comes as US federal debt stands above $40tn, with the Treasury expected to reach its borrowing limit around the middle of 2027 on its current trajectory. Congress will then face pressure to raise or suspend the ceiling, setting up another potentially bruising political confrontation over government finances.
A Democratic victory in the House of Representatives would give the party greater leverage in negotiations, while control of the Senate as well would strengthen its position considerably.
Green argues that both parties would enter the negotiations with expensive political demands. Republicans would seek additional defence funding, while Democrats would push to reverse Medicaid cuts included in last year’s budget legislation.
“Both sides will arrive at the table wanting something expensive,” he said.
“Republicans want more money for defence. Democrats want to reverse the Medicaid cuts in last year’s budget law. In today’s Washington, nobody wants to be seen to blink, so the likeliest compromise gives each side what it wants and leaves the Treasury to borrow the difference.”
Some estimates suggest a settlement along those lines could increase the US deficit by around 1 per cent of gross domestic product.
That prospect could create a volatile pattern for bond markets. Treasury prices may initially rise and yields fall after the election, only for investors to reassess the country’s fiscal outlook as the debt-ceiling deadline approaches and the cost of securing a political agreement becomes clearer.
Green said the concern was not simply the additional borrowing, but what repeated fiscal compromises would signal to investors about Washington’s willingness to control its finances.
“If every compromise in Washington ends with a bigger deficit, lenders will want paying more to hold long-dated US debt,” he said.
“Long-term borrowing costs go up, the yield curve steepens, and once that gets going it can get away from policymakers very quickly.”
The implications would extend well beyond the US government bond market. Long-term Treasury yields help determine borrowing costs across the global economy, influencing mortgage rates, corporate financing and the valuations investors place on equities.
Higher yields can make future company earnings less attractive in present-value terms, placing particular pressure on highly valued growth and technology stocks. Businesses also face more expensive financing, while households can find mortgage borrowing increasingly costly.
“Long-dated Treasury yields feed into almost everything,” Green said. “Mortgage rates, company borrowing costs, and share valuations all take their cue from them. When they climb for the wrong reasons, highly valued growth stocks usually feel it first.”
He believes the bond market could ultimately have a greater influence on investment performance in 2027 than the sector-by-sector consequences of a Democratic victory.
The prospect of renewed concerns over US fiscal discipline could also strengthen demand for assets traditionally viewed as alternatives to government-issued money and conventional financial markets.
Gold has long attracted investors seeking protection against political and monetary uncertainty, while Bitcoin has increasingly been promoted by supporters as an alternative store of value. Green expects both could benefit if Washington becomes embroiled in a prolonged funding dispute.
“When doubts grow about how a government handles its finances, investors look for places to put money that sit beyond its reach,” he said.
“Gold has long played that role, and Bitcoin increasingly does too. A drawn-out fight over America’s debt would, in my view, likely strengthen the case for both as part of a diversified approach.”
Even a Democratic sweep of Congress would not remove the president’s veto powers or broad executive authority. It would, however, constrain the White House’s legislative freedom and potentially intensify negotiations over spending and borrowing.
For investors, Green’s central warning is that an initial market rally should not be mistaken for an improvement in America’s long-term fiscal position.
“America has always been able to borrow on the strength of its name,” he said.
“Every funding fight that ends in a bigger bill spends a little of that reputation, and it’s far harder to earn back than it is to lose.”

articles.title: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh Just Drove a Dagger Through Wall Street's AI-Driven Rally With 6 Blunt Words - The Motley Fool
articles.summary: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh Just Drove a Dagger Through Wall Street's AI-Driven Rally With 6 Blunt Words  The Motley Fool
articles.full_text:
For the better part of the last four years, the Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI +3.03%), S&P 500 (^GSPC +1.58%), and Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC +1.44%) have been virtually unstoppable, thanks in large part to the evolution of artificial intelligence (AI).
Empowering software and systems with the tools to make autonomous, split-second decisions promises to increase productivity and efficiency for most sectors and industries, and is widely viewed as a can't-miss investment opportunity. But AI stocks aren't infallible, at least according to Fed Chair Kevin Warsh.
Fed Chair Kevin Warsh just leveled with investors about AI stocks. Image source: Official Federal Reserve Photo.
On Oct. 28, Warsh and his Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) colleagues voted to hold interest rates steady amid a 67th consecutive month of annualized inflation above the Fed's long-term 2% target. While the FOMC's decision often dominates the headlines, it's Fed Chair Warsh's commentary with the press following the October FOMC meeting that's truly stirring the pot.
With just six blunt words, the head of the Federal Reserve drove a dagger through the stock market's No. 1 catalyst.
AI stocks aren't immune to rising interest rates
Following every FOMC rate-decision meeting, the sitting Fed chair delivers prepared remarks and then fields a handful of questions from the press.
Since taking over as Fed chair on May 22, Warsh has done away with forward-looking guidance in FOMC meeting statements and in his post-meeting discussions with reporters. In other words, getting direct answers or hints about what's to come has been challenging during Warsh's five-month tenure.
But in one of his more candid moments since succeeding Jerome Powell, Fed Chair Warsh opened up about the interest-rate sensitivity of AI companies:
Interest rates get in the cracks, interest rates affect directly or indirectly, almost everything... You've seen market participants that are discriminating between the kinds of investments they want to make. You've seen credit spreads for certain assets widen out, gap out. For others, you've seen some tightening in financial conditions, but not significantly.
It's this blunt six-word assessment, "interest rates get in the cracks," that's sent an unmistakable message to AI stock investors.
While some of Wall Street's hyperscalers are funding their data center build-outs through stock issuances and cash on hand, the otherworldly demand for AI hardware is being financed, in part, with debt. If borrowing costs continue to climb, they could adversely affect this expansion and near-term growth projections, forcing a re-rating of the second-priciest stock market in history.
Image source: Getty Images.
AI stocks may face interest rate pressure on two fronts
What makes the current interest rate climate especially tricky for AI stocks is that they could be hammered on two fronts.
The most obvious is that Warsh and the FOMC are expected to raise interest rates several times, beginning in December. The CME Group's (CME +1.39%) FedWatch Tool predicts a 72% chance of a 25-basis-point rate hike in December and a nearly 50% chance of 75 basis points in cumulative hikes by Sept. 15, 2027.
The last time US Treasury yields were this high, total US national debt stood at just $8.9 trillion. Today, US debt stands at $40.1 trillion. That's +$31.2 trillion more, or over 4.5 TIMES higher. This means every 1 percentage point in the average cost of servicing the debt now translates to ~$401 billion per year in interest expense. In 2007, the same 1 percentage point translated to just ~$89 billion. That’s an additional ~$312 BILLION in annual interest expense for every percentage point increase in borrowing cost. This is a vastly different situation than it was 19 years ago. The bond market matters more now than ever.
— The Kobeissi Letter (@KobeissiLetter) September 25, 2026
But the bond market may also punish AI stocks. Notably higher long-duration Treasury bond yields (specifically 10- and 30-year yields) can increase corporate borrowing costs. While elevated inflation is one reason long-duration Treasury yields have surged in 2026, it's not the only one. For instance, bond traders are also concerned about U.S. total debt surpassing $40 trillion and ongoing federal deficits.
This combination of forces pushing up lending rates is a potential disaster in the making for AI stocks.

articles.title: Swiss Franc builds momentum as inflation data approaches - www.tmgm.com
articles.summary: Swiss Franc builds momentum as inflation data approaches  www.tmgm.com
articles.full_text:
Support for the Swiss Franc (CHF) ahead of Switzerland’s Consumer Price Index (CPI) release is keeping USD/CHF under pressure. Having surrendered its gains for the day, the pair is trading broadly unchanged near 0.8180 during Tuesday’s Asian session. Monthly Swiss inflation is forecast to hold at 0% in October, while annual CPI inflation is expected to rise to 1.3% from 1.0% previously.
Swiss economic releases on Monday offered contrasting signals. Real Retail Sales increased 1.6% year-on-year in September, the weakest rise since March, against forecasts of 3%. This followed an upwardly revised 3.9% gain in August. Manufacturing, however, remained stronger: the SVME Manufacturing Purchasing Managers Index (PMI) advanced from September’s 55.3 to 56.7 in October. The reading beat market expectations of 55.3 and marked an eighth consecutive month of expansion.
Weakness in the US Dollar (USD) ahead of the US midterm elections erased USD/CHF’s gains for the day. Elevated energy prices associated with ongoing conflicts with Iran have intensified political pressure on US President Donald Trump and the Republican Party. Prediction markets, meanwhile, assign a 74% probability to the Democratic Party taking control of the US Senate, underscoring the high political stakes of the vote.
Also in focus is the US jobs report due later this week, which market participants will scrutinise for fresh indications of labour market conditions and implications for future monetary policy decisions. With the Federal Reserve retaining its hawkish stance, the CME FedWatch Tool currently indicates roughly a 73% probability of a December rate hike following October’s policy pause.
For Commerzbank’s Norman Liebke, the US midterm result remains relevant to the Dollar’s near-term outlook, even though it is just one of several influences. Noting that “the election result is unlikely to be entirely irrelevant for the dollar,” he cautions that a Republican loss of majorities in both chambers would mean “the dollar could come under greater pressure, as the Trump administration would have less political backing overall.” Even a narrower change in Washington would have implications, Liebke adds: “If only the House of Representatives changes hands, the dollar would likely face some headwinds as well, albeit to a lesser extent.”
As Switzerland’s official currency, the Swiss Franc (CHF) ranks among the ten most actively traded currencies worldwide, with trading volumes far exceeding the size of the Swiss economy. Broader market sentiment, domestic economic conditions and Swiss National Bank (SNB) decisions are among the factors influencing its value. From 2011 to 2015, the Franc was pegged to the Euro (EUR). Its abrupt removal sent the Franc more than 20% higher and triggered market turmoil. Although that peg no longer applies, the Swiss economy’s heavy reliance on the neighbouring Eurozone means CHF movements still tend to track those of the Euro closely.
Investors often turn to the Swiss Franc (CHF) during periods of market stress, giving it the status of a safe-haven asset. Switzerland’s reputation rests on its stable economy, strong export sector, substantial central bank reserves and longstanding policy of neutrality in global conflicts. These characteristics make its currency attractive to investors seeking to reduce risk. During turbulent periods, CHF is likely to appreciate against currencies regarded as riskier investments.
Monetary policy decisions at the Swiss National Bank (SNB) are taken four times a year, once each quarter, a less frequent schedule than at other major central banks. Its objective is annual inflation below 2%. If inflation exceeds the target, or is projected to do so in the foreseeable future, the SNB will seek to curb price increases by raising its policy rate. Such rate increases generally support the Swiss Franc (CHF): higher yields make Switzerland more attractive to investors. Lower interest rates, by contrast, typically put pressure on CHF.
Switzerland’s macroeconomic releases help investors gauge the economy’s condition and can influence the valuation of the Swiss Franc (CHF). Despite the economy’s broad stability, abrupt shifts in growth, inflation, the current account or central bank currency reserves can prompt CHF movements. Strong economic growth, low unemployment and buoyant confidence generally support the currency. Data signalling a loss of economic momentum, on the other hand, is likely to lead to CHF depreciation.
Switzerland’s small, open economy relies heavily on the economic health of its Eurozone neighbours. With the broader European Union serving as its main economic partner and an important political ally, stability in Eurozone macroeconomic conditions and monetary policy is crucial for Switzerland and, in turn, the Swiss Franc (CHF). Reflecting this dependence, some models put the correlation between the fortunes of the Euro (EUR) and CHF at more than 90%, close to a perfect correlation.

articles.title: China Securities Regulatory Commission Vice Chairman Li Chao: China to Accelerate New Round of Capital Market Reform and Opening, RMB Stock Trading Counters to Be Included in Stock Connect - BigGo Finance
articles.summary: China Securities Regulatory Commission Vice Chairman Li Chao: China to Accelerate New Round of Capital Market Reform and Opening, RMB Stock Trading Counters to Be Included in Stock Connect  BigGo Finance
articles.full_text:
On the morning of November 3, Li Chao, Vice Chairman of the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC), delivered a keynote speech at the fifth Global Financial Leaders' Investment Summit hosted by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, laying out in detail the direction of reform and opening measures for mainland China's capital market in the next stage. He said the CSRC will implement the arrangements of China's 15th Five-Year Plan, push deeper for the New Nine Guidelines and the capital market's "1+N" policy framework to take effect, and, guided by comprehensive reform of investment and financing, accelerate a new round of capital market reform and opening while improving market functions that coordinate investment and financing.
Li Chao described the CSRC's regulatory progress in mainland China's capital market this year across five dimensions. Safeguarding the stable operation of the market was placed first. He noted that in the face of multiple greater-than-expected imported risks, the CSRC has continued to strengthen monitoring and market-stabilization mechanisms, further improved the institutional ecosystem for "long money and long-term investment," advanced reform of publicly offered funds, and steadily raised both the scale and share of medium- and long-term capital from social security funds, annuities and insurers entering the market.
On improving the quality and investment value of listed companies, Li Chao's figures showed that in the first three quarters of this year, Chinese listed companies carried out nearly 2,000 M&A and restructuring deals worth close to 1.5 trillion yuan (approximately $225 billion), through which a group of quality enterprises accelerated their transformation and upgrading. Over the same period, revenue and profits of A-share listed companies showed sound growth, dividend and buyback amounts far exceeded IPO and refinancing proceeds, and investors' awareness of and capacity for returns steadily strengthened.
Inclusive reform has focused on serving new quality productive forces. This year the CSRC rolled out measures including optimizing the refinancing system and mechanism and deepening ChiNext reform, and expanded the scope of the STAR Market's fifth set of listing standards to the artificial intelligence field, helping a group of representative companies in new quality productive forces list efficiently and driving the development of industrial cluster advantages.
On supervision and enforcement, the CSRC has for three consecutive years run special campaigns against financial fraud, while cracking down on illegal cross-border business conducted by overseas securities firms, promoting the release of guidelines for high-quality development of private funds, and improving institutional rules such as advance compensation, so as to better protect the lawful rights and interests of small and medium-sized investors.
On opening up, in the first three quarters of 2026 the CSRC completed overseas listing filings for more than 130 companies, supporting enterprises in making good use of both markets and both resources; it supported the smooth listing in Hong Kong of five-year RMB government bond futures and allowed qualified foreign institutional investors (QFII) to participate in trading of mainland China government bond futures. The CSRC also recently approved the establishment of Citi Securities China, bringing the number of wholly foreign-owned securities firms to seven.
On cooperation between the mainland China and Hong Kong capital markets, Li Chao said consolidating and enhancing Hong Kong's status as an international financial center is a major national strategy. The CSRC will deepen two-way opening in accordance with the "five synergies" cooperation model proposed by CSRC Chairman Wu Qing in Hong Kong in August this year.
Specific measures include: accelerating the inclusion of RMB stock trading counters and real estate investment trusts (REITs) in Stock Connect, implementing the optimized QFII scheme, and supporting mainland Chinese companies seeking to expand internationally to list in Hong Kong; advancing high-level opening of the equity, bond and futures markets in a coordinated way, developing more indexes linked to Chinese assets and ETF products aligned with China's modern industrial system; deepening cross-border regulatory cooperation with Hong Kong regulators, strengthening monitoring and identification of cross-border capital flow risks, and enhancing information sharing and regulatory coordination on emerging businesses such as tokenization of real-world assets; and deeply participating in the formulation of international rules for global capital markets.
"At present, China's economy is showing sound momentum of new drivers and improved structure. The safety value, resilience value and innovation value of China's capital market are steadily drawing attention and recognition from all sides," Li Chao said.
On the same day, China's three major A-share indexes all closed lower, with the Shanghai Composite down 0.82%, the Shenzhen Component down 1.21% and the ChiNext Index down 2.73%. Combined turnover across the Shanghai, Shenzhen and Beijing markets exceeded 1.7 trillion yuan (approximately $255 billion), shrinking by nearly 100 billion yuan from the previous trading day. Sector performance diverged, with medical aesthetics, insurance, rare earths and airlines and airports among the top gainers, while components, semiconductors, communications equipment and robotics lagged.
On the policy front, the CSRC on November 2 released a series of policies to stabilize the market and expectations in the form of answers to reporters' questions, covering two structural monetary policy tools, enriching market investment tools, adjusting and optimizing buyback rules aimed at supporting the market, and giving play to the countercyclical role of margin trading and securities lending. The People's Bank of China announced the same day that on November 3 it conducted swap facility operations for securities, fund and insurance companies totaling 100 billion yuan (approximately $15.0 billion) at a winning rate of 10 basis points, with 31 institutions bidding; it also announced that from November 15 it will raise the foreign exchange deposit reserve ratio for financial institutions to 6% from 4%.
Galaxy Securities analysis holds that the seesaw effect between dividend assets and technology growth sectors is currently pronounced, volatility in the tech sector is rising, and a pattern of range-bound rotation that trades time for space may remain a阶段性 feature; it recommends a "barbell" strategy balancing flexible assets against defensive core holdings. Shenwan Hongyuan noted that after the continued adjustment, conditions for an oversold rebound have improved further, and an important medium- to long-term low may appear around the turn of the year. Founder Securities judges that after entering November, negative factors will gradually ease, risk appetite is expected to improve, and the market will shift from defense to offense.
Judging from Li Chao's remarks, regulators are trying to build an institutional balance between "stability" and "progress": on one hand, shoring up the market floor through medium- and long-term capital entry and buyback and dividend mechanisms; on the other, opening up incremental space through M&A and restructuring, inclusive STAR Market reform and expansion of Stock Connect. If RMB stock trading counters are included in Stock Connect, it would give overseas investors a channel that avoids currency conversion, providing a substantive boost to RMB internationalization and to the RMB-denominated ecosystem in Hong Kong stocks; and the inclusion of REITs in mutual market access is expected to bring overseas long-term allocation capital into mainland China's infrastructure assets. The expansion of wholly foreign-owned securities firms to seven also signals that the pace of opening up the financial sector has not slowed. For investors, the short-term market remains constrained by factors such as divergent earnings from overseas tech stocks and geopolitical disruptions, but the density and rhythm of the policy toolkit are building conditions for a valuation recovery around the turn of the year.

articles.title: WTI Price Forecast: US-Iran peace hopes limit upside as price holds modest gains above $96.00 - www.tmgm.com

articles.full_text:
Trading above $96.00, West Texas Intermediate (WTI), the US crude oil benchmark, is up over 1.0% on Tuesday as buyers return during the Asian session. The advance recovers some of the previous day's sharp fall towards $94.30, a low not seen for over two weeks, against a backdrop of mixed developments in the Middle East crisis.
Despite Tehran's revised proposals to reopen the strategic Strait of Hormuz for two days, several days of talks between Iranian officials and Qatari mediators produced no major breakthrough. A geopolitical risk premium therefore remains embedded in oil prices, providing some support. However, talks between the US and Iran are reportedly continuing. US President Donald Trump also said on Monday that Iran wants a deal to end the war and that an agreement could be reached.
Further encouragement for diplomacy came from Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian, who said Tehran is looking to resolve problems through dialogue. His comments bolster hopes of a diplomatic settlement to end the eight-month war, potentially restricting any substantial advance in crude oil prices. Strong follow-through buying would therefore be needed before fresh bullish positions could prudently be taken in anticipation of a resumption of the established uptrend seen over roughly the past four months.
With prices holding above all key Fibonacci retracement support levels, the near-term technical outlook for oil remains bullish. Immediate support now lies at the 23.6% retracement of $95.18. Momentum signals nevertheless warrant caution: the Relative Strength Index, close to 50.0, points to neutral pressure, while the Moving Average Convergence Divergence (MACD) has turned marginally negative. As long as crude oil remains above these underlying levels, the latest retreat appears more consistent with consolidation than a reversal of the trend.
At $103.87, the recent cycle high and Fibonacci anchor forms the next major resistance level. A decisive move through it would clear the way for the prevailing bullish trend to extend. Below current prices, the 23.6% Fibonacci retracement at $95.18 provides initial support. A wider zone of demand follows around the 38.2% retracement at $89.81 and the 100-day SMA at $85.86, with the nearby 50.0% retracement at $85.46 lending further strength to that medium-term base. A steeper fall would bring the 61.8% retracement at $81.12 into view, followed by the lower Fibonacci levels of $74.93 and $67.05.
(The technical analysis of this story was written with the help of an AI tool. Know more.)
Traded internationally, WTI Oil takes its name from West Texas Intermediate and is one of three major crude oil types alongside Brent and Dubai Crude. Its relatively low gravity and sulphur content account for its descriptions as “light” and “sweet”, respectively. This high-quality oil is considered easy to refine. Produced in the United States, it is distributed through the Cushing hub, known as “The Pipeline Crossroads of the World”. WTI serves as an oil market benchmark, with its price regularly cited in media reports.
Supply and demand underpin WTI Oil prices, as they do those of other assets. Stronger global growth can lift demand, while weaker growth can have the reverse effect. Supply disruptions caused by political instability, wars or sanctions can also affect prices. Another major influence is the policy of OPEC, the group of leading oil-producing countries. Since oil is traded predominantly in US dollars, the currency's value also matters: a weaker US dollar can make oil more affordable, whereas a stronger dollar can have the opposite effect.
WTI Oil prices respond to the weekly inventory reports from the American Petroleum Institute (API) and the Energy Information Agency (EIA), as changes in stocks reveal shifts in supply and demand. Falling inventories may signal stronger demand and lift oil prices; rising stocks may indicate greater supply and weigh on prices. The API releases its report each Tuesday, followed by the EIA the next day. The two sets of figures are generally similar, coming within 1% of one another 75% of the time. As the EIA is a government agency, its figures are regarded as more reliable.
At meetings held twice a year, the 12 oil-producing nations that make up OPEC (Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries) jointly set production quotas for member countries. These decisions frequently influence WTI Oil prices. Lower quotas can constrain supply and raise oil prices, while increased OPEC production can have the reverse effect. The wider OPEC+ group brings in ten additional non-OPEC members, most notably Russia.

articles.title: Bank of England set to hike interest rates to tackle higher inflation caused by Iran war - AOL.com
articles.summary: Bank of England set to hike interest rates to tackle higher inflation caused by Iran war  AOL.com
articles.full_text:
LONDON (AP) — The Bank of England is expected to raise interest rates Thursday for the first time in over three years in order to tackle the inflation shock caused by the Iran war.
With inflation predicted to rise further over the coming months, economists reckon the nine policymakers on the Monetary Policy Committee have little option but to increase the bank's key rate to 4% from 3.75%. The anticipated increase would be the first since August 2023.
The pressure on rate-setters has grown steadily over recent months, but the rise in inflation to an 11-month high of 3.5% in September — above their target of 2% — cemented market expectations of a rate hike this month and potentially more in 2027.
The main cause behind the spike in inflation this year has been the sharp rise in fuel costs as a result of the Iran war and the ensuing bottlenecks in the Strait of Hormuz, which have squeezed global oil and gas supplies.
Advertisement
“We imagine that many committee members’ patience with the recent rise in inflation has worn thin," said Ellie Henderson, an economist at Investec. “The longer energy prices remain elevated, the greater the risk that a temporary price shock becomes more permanent."
Accompanying the expected rate hike will be the bank’s quarterly economic projections, notably those for inflation and growth. Higher interest rates cool the economy by making it more expensive to borrow, thereby bearing down on spending and inflation, but growth too.
Other central banks, including the U.S. Federal Reserve and the European Central Bank, have raised rates recently in response to rising prices.
Interest rates in the U.K. had been trending downward from a 15-year high of 5.25% until the U.S. and Israel attacked Iran in late February.
