articles.title: Bank of England set to hike interest rates to 4% to tackle rising inflation - Herts Advertiser
articles.summary: Bank of England set to hike interest rates to 4% to tackle rising inflation  Herts Advertiser
articles.full_text:
The Bank of England is poised to hike interest rates for the first time in more than three years, economists think.
Rate-setters are widely expected to tighten monetary policy in a bid to tackle rising inflation in the UK economy.
Traders in the financial markets are predicting that rates will increase to 4% from 3.75% when the Bank’s Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) announces its next decision on Thursday.
This would be the first time that the central bank increases borrowing costs since August 2023, and means that mortgage holders could be facing a squeeze.
Pressure on the MPC to take action has grown since official figures showed the rate of Consumer Prices Index (CPI) inflation rose to 3.5% in September, the highest level in 11 months.
The conflict in the Middle East has helped push CPI further away from the Bank’s 2% target rate, with a surge in petrol and diesel prices a major driving force.
And inflation is expected to be pushed higher this winter after Ofgem’s energy price cap rose by 3.6% for a typical household on October 1 and is forecast to jump by a further 22% in January.
Ellie Henderson, an analyst for Investec, said: “We imagine that many committee members’ patience with the recent rise in inflation has worn thin.
“The longer energy prices remain elevated, the greater the risk that a temporary price shock becomes more permanent; a ‘risk management’ hike could guard against this.”
She cautioned that producers might “not be willing or able to shoulder the burden of higher energy prices for much longer” and that this could push up prices in shops.
Alexander Harvey, UK economist for Oxford Economics, said a November rate hike looks to be a “done deal” for the committee, which will be responding to higher oil and gas prices.
“So far, two factors have been central to the MPC’s decision-making since the outbreak of the conflict in the Middle East: the scale and duration of the energy price shock, plus the extent of any second-round inflation effects from elevated energy prices,” he said.
“These factors will continue to dominate the outlook for Bank rate.”
He said the key thing economists will be looking out for is any signal from the Bank as to where interest rates could go from here, with the financial markets expecting further hikes into 2027.
Other central banks have already increased their interest rates, including the US Federal Reserve which did so last month for the first time in three years.
The MPC will also take into account other economic indicators including that the UK’s unemployment rate fell to the lowest level in more than a year in the three months to August, to 4.7%.
Furthermore, the economy unexpectedly grew in August, by 0.1%, suggesting resilience in the UK despite pressure on consumer spending and wider volatility because of the Iran war.

articles.title: Bank of England poised to raise rate as inflation jumps - Bangkok Post
articles.summary: Bank of England poised to raise rate as inflation jumps  Bangkok Post
articles.full_text:
LONDON - The Bank of England is expected to raise its benchmark interest rate on Thursday for the first time in more than three years as soaring energy costs push up global inflation.
The BoE is forecast to tighten borrowing costs by a quarter point to 4.0%, finally catching up with the US Federal Reserve and European Central Bank in tightening borrowing costs since the start of the Middle East conflict.
Along with Ukraine’s strikes on Russian refineries, disruptions to energy supplies owing to the US-Iran war has caused record-high diesel prices around the world.
“Borrowers are braced for at least one rate hike” from the BoE this year as “consumer confidence has been jarred by the prospect of prices edging ever higher in the wake of the ongoing conflict in the Middle East”, noted Danni Hewson, head of financial analysis at AJ Bell.
The BoE last raised its rate in August 2023 and has kept the cost of borrowing at 3.75% since December.
Latest official data showed Britain’s annual inflation rate accelerated by more than expected in September, rising to 3.5% on surging fuel prices.
UK inflation is forecast to hit around four percent in the new year with millions of Britons facing a jump in energy bills, even after the government offered some assistance in its annual budget announcement last week.
Alongside its monetary policy update, the BoE will reveal its latest forecasts for UK economic growth and inflation, which analysts expect to come in similar to recent estimates from the country’s Labour government and International Monetary Fund.
Both said last month that they expect Britain’s economy to have grown this year before slowing in 2027.
“We expect the Bank to raise its forecasts for near-term growth and inflation in its monetary policy report, but higher energy prices could ultimately weigh on its growth forecasts further ahead,” said Nomura analyst George Buckley.
Australia’s central bank raised its key interest rate to an 18-year high of 4.85% on Tuesday, citing the prolonged war in the Middle East and persistent inflationary pressures.

At 8:00 PM, local Cuban time, the wraps up the day this Wednesday, November 4, 2026, showing mixed signals: the U.S. dollar increases and solidifies its upward trend, while the euro loses some momentum compared to the previous session.
The MLC, with a low volume of operations, shows a sharp movement that should be considered as an indicative value.
The dollar continues to rise
The U.S. dollar is priced at 915 Cuban pesos (CUP) at the close of this trading day, with a buying rate around 910 CUP and a selling rate of about 920 CUP.
This represents an increase of 5 pesos compared to the previous day, when the average value was 910 CUP. The trend is clear and sustained: seven days ago, the dollar was at 858 CUP, indicating a rise of 57.5 pesos in a week, equivalent to an increase of 6.7%.
The 30-day comparison shows an increase of 145 pesos—an 18.8%—although this figure may partially reflect adjustments in the index methodology. In the past 30 days, the dollar has reached a high of 915 CUP and a low of 768 CUP. The demand for dollars remains high among those looking to protect their savings against the depreciation of the peso.
Exchange Rate Evolution
The euro is loosening its grip but continues to dominate
The euro closes at 996 Cuban pesos (CUP), with a buy price of 992 CUP and a sell price of 999 CUP. Compared to the previous day, the average value rises by just 1.5 pesos —0.2%— which effectively means a virtually flat exchange rate with a slight retreat from the intraday highs.
In the last week, the euro has gained 55.5 pesos, a 5.9% increase from the 940 CUP it was seven days ago.
The maximum of the last 30 days coincides with today's closing: 996 CUP, while the minimum for the period was 860 CUP. It exceeds the dollar by 81 pesos, consolidating its dominant position in the Cuban parallel market.
The MLC, with indicative data
The MLC closes with an average value of 758 Cuban pesos (CUP), with a buying price of 698 CUP and a selling price of 818 CUP. This figure represents an increase of 70 pesos compared to the previous session —a 10.2% rise— and an increase of 66.5 pesos since today's opening.
However, the data for this currency is marked with a warning of low trading volume, so the value should be taken as indicative and with caution.
In the last 30 days, the MLC has fluctuated between a minimum of 496 CUP and the current maximum of 758 CUP. Without physical existence, its use is limited to the state-owned businesses that accept it, which restricts its circulation compared to cash currencies.
Summary of exchange rates as of the close on November 4, 2026
- Exchange rate of the dollar USD to CUP: 915 CUP.
- Exchange rate of the euro EUR to CUP: 996 CUP.
- Exchange rate from MLC to CUP: 758 CUP (indicative value, limited data).
The official exchange rate of the Central Bank of Cuba (Segment III) is 781 CUP per dollar and 874 CUP per euro, remaining well below the rates that prevail in everyday practice in the informal currency market.
Although Segment III was introduced as a more flexible exchange mechanism, its official rate remains far from that of the informal market and fails to meet the actual demand for foreign currency from the population.
The gap between the official and informal rates for the dollar exceeds 134 pesos; for the euro, it exceeds 122 pesos.
The gap between the official and informal exchange rates reflects the ongoing scarcity of foreign currency in the state banking system and the high demand for dollars and euros by the population, whether for emigration, importing goods, protecting savings, or making purchases in the private sector.
In a scenario of sustained inflation, low state wages, and increasing partial dollarization of the economy, every change in the informal market directly affects internal prices and the purchasing power of Cubans.
The Exchange Rate of CiberCuba is an index of the informal Cuban market created through automated analysis of thousands of currency exchange postings on Telegram and Facebook groups; the calculation excludes atypical offers and spam messages, weighs each transaction according to its age, and consolidates a representative value that is updated multiple times a day.

articles.title: BoJ Minutes: Members agree it was suitable for bank to keep increasing policy interest rate - www.tmgm.com
articles.summary: BoJ Minutes: Members agree it was suitable for bank to keep increasing policy interest rate  www.tmgm.com
articles.full_text:
The Bank of Japan (BoJ) board members shared their views on the monetary policy outlook on Thursday, per the BoJ Minutes of the September meeting.
Members concurred it was suitable for the bank to keep increasing the policy interest rate and modify the level of monetary easing.
One member said it was preferable for the bank to move the policy interest rate closer to the target relatively soon and maintain flexibility for quick adjustments in either direction.
One member said it was important to show the market BOJ's resolve to prevent upward price deviations with agile response to global economic conditions. 
Cabinet Office rep expects central bank to fulfill accountability on meeting decisions and closely examine cumulative effects of past rate policies. 
One member noted that if signs of rising price deviation appeared, the bank would need to speed up rate hikes. 
The Bank of Japan (BoJ) is the Japanese central bank, which sets monetary policy in the country. Its mandate is to issue banknotes and carry out currency and monetary control to ensure price stability, which means an inflation target of around 2%.
The Bank of Japan embarked in an ultra-loose monetary policy in 2013 in order to stimulate the economy and fuel inflation amid a low-inflationary environment. The bank’s policy is based on Quantitative and Qualitative Easing (QQE), or printing notes to buy assets such as government or corporate bonds to provide liquidity. In 2016, the bank doubled down on its strategy and further loosened policy by first introducing negative interest rates and then directly controlling the yield of its 10-year government bonds. In March 2024, the BoJ lifted interest rates, effectively retreating from the ultra-loose monetary policy stance.
The Bank’s massive stimulus caused the Yen to depreciate against its main currency peers. This process exacerbated in 2022 and 2023 due to an increasing policy divergence between the Bank of Japan and other main central banks, which opted to increase interest rates sharply to fight decades-high levels of inflation. The BoJ’s policy led to a widening differential with other currencies, dragging down the value of the Yen. This trend partly reversed in 2024, when the BoJ decided to abandon its ultra-loose policy stance.
A weaker Yen and the spike in global energy prices led to an increase in Japanese inflation, which exceeded the BoJ’s 2% target. The prospect of rising salaries in the country – a key element fuelling inflation – also contributed to the move.

articles.title: CVS Health to split pharmacy chain from health insurance
articles.summary: CVS Pharmacy will be separate from CVS Health, housing major insurer Aetna and benefits manager CaremarkCVS Health, the largest US healthcare conglomerate valued at $117bn, has announced its plans split off its pharmacy chain from its health insurance and benefits businesses, ending an era in which healthcare companies grew into vast conglomerates.In their announcement on Wednesday, CVS Health said they will split off its 9,000 pharmacies, in-store clinics and mail order prescription business in...
articles.full_text:
CVS Health, the largest US healthcare conglomerate valued at $117bn, has announced its plans split off its pharmacy chain from its health insurance and benefits businesses, ending an era in which healthcare companies grew into vast conglomerates.
In their announcement on Wednesday, CVS Health said they will split off its 9,000 pharmacies, in-store clinics and mail order prescription business into a business named CVS Pharmacy.
A second company will keep the name CVS Health and house the major insurer Aetna and the giant pharmacy benefits manager Caremark, along with other businesses that provide home visits and primary care to older people.
The company has come under pressure from lawmakers and regulators over concerns that the healthcare giants, including CVS Health, UnitedHealth Group and Cigna, have become too dominant, leading to higher medical costs. The three companies control roughly 80% of the market. CVS Health in particular generated over $400bn in revenue last year.
A political pushback against healthcare gigantism has led Arkansas and Tennessee to pass laws aimed at preventing the companies from managing prescription benefits and running retail and mail-order pharmacies.
The Arkansas state representative Jeremiah Moore, a Republican who sponsored the state’s bill, told Politico last week: “The average American citizen is really tired of being pushed around and bullied, whether it be from the government or a monopolistic company.”
He added: “For far too long, they’ve taken advantage of these sick people, and it’s what I consider to be crony capitalism. They’re bending the rules to benefit their own bottom line.” Other states have proposed similar restrictions.
At the federal level, a bill introduced by the Missouri Republican senator Josh Hawley and Massachusetts senator Elizabeth Warren proposes an antitrust crackdown.
Hawley has described the legislation as “a major step toward restoring transparency and making healthcare more affordable for every American.”
David Joyner, CVS’s chief executive and chair, will run the healthcare solutions business.
 
“Our history is defined by proactively evolving to stay ahead of what’s next in healthcare, and in today’s environment, that means delivering more affordability, greater access and a simpler experience,” said Joyner in a statement.
That marks a stark turnaround from CVS Health’s earlier opposition to legislative efforts to break up the healthcare giant, which a company spokesman said would “open the door to private equity stripping the entire U.S. healthcare system for parts”.
The announcement comes after a series of acquisitions that saw CVS Health expand into nearly every corner of the healthcare system. It began in 2018, when CVS and Aetna merged in a $70bn deal. Healthcare rivals, UnitedHealth and Cigna, also brought into the trend of harnessing an insurer, pharmacy benefits, and a mail-order business under one operation.
CVS Health, however, did not meet investors’ expectations for growth. In late 2024, its share price fell to $44, though it has since rebounded. The CVS Health breakup is planned for early 2028.
